title: P versus NP
summary: P versus NP asks whether every problem with efficiently checkable solutions also has an efficient deterministic decision algorithm. Boolean satisfiability is a representative test case because all NP problems reduce to it. Checking one assignment is easy, while deciding whether any assignment works requires accounting for all possibilities. The target concerns worst-case polynomial time on arbitrarily large inputs. A resolution would establish a fundamental relationship between searching and verifying, without by itself determining practical exponents or average-case difficulty.
formal: Does every language in \(\mathrm{NP}\) belong to \(\mathrm{P}\)? Equivalently, is there a deterministic Turing machine \(A\) and fixed constants \(C,k\ge1\) such that \(A\) decides SAT on every input of \(N\) bits in at most \(C(N+1)^k\) steps?
definitions: Use the shared definitions of [P and NP](definitions.html#p-np), [SAT](definitions.html#sat) and [uniform bit computation](definitions.html#bit-model). Here \(N\) is the complete bit length of the input formula, including its tree structure, variable identifiers and delimiters. Fix an ordinary explicit binary encoding of formulas over AND, OR and NOT, and reject malformed strings. Polynomially interconvertible ordinary encodings give the same P-versus-NP question; this does not assert an unchanged polynomial exponent under every encoding. No oracle, advice or random error is allowed.
answer_criterion: Prove \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\) or \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{NP}\) in the deterministic uniform model defined here. Equality requires that every NP language have a polynomial-time decision algorithm; inequality requires that at least one NP language have none.

title: Superlinear Boolean circuit lower bounds
summary: The question asks for a polynomial-time computable function with as many output bits as input bits that needs more than linear circuit size. Competing circuits may use every two-input Boolean operation and share intermediate work without depth or fan-out restrictions. The lower-bound ratio must be unbounded at arbitrarily large input lengths, not necessarily tend to infinity at every length. Known explicit full-basis lower bounds improve fixed linear constants, and recent conditional barriers apply only to specified proof classes. A complete answer must prove or refute the existence of one uniformly computable function satisfying the entire claim.
formal:
Does there exist one total, length-preserving, deterministic polynomial-time function
\[F:\{0,1\}^{*}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{*},\qquad |F(x)|=|x|,\]
whose unrestricted Boolean circuit complexity is not linear? Precisely, writing \(F_n:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}^{n}\) for its restriction to inputs of length \(n\), the requested lower bound is
\[\forall C>0\ \forall n_0\ge1\ \exists n\ge n_0:\quad \operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(F_n)>Cn.\]
Here \(C\) is real and \(n_0,n\) are integers. The same uniform algorithm computes all \(n\) outputs of \(F_n\) at every length. The lower bound need only exceed every fixed linear bound at arbitrarily large lengths.
definitions:
Length preservation requires exactly \(n\) output bits on an \(n\)-bit input, including the empty output on the empty input. Use the [uniform bit model](definitions.html#bit-model). One deterministic multitape machine computes \(F(x)\) within \(a(|x|+1)^d\) steps for a fixed real \(a\ge1\) and integer \(d\ge1\), including the time to write the output.

Use the [Boolean circuit convention](definitions.html#boolean-circuits) with the full \(B_2\) basis and free constants. The circuit has \(n\) inputs and \(n\) ordered output wires, with unrestricted fan-out, sharing and depth. All outputs are computed jointly; an output may directly select an input or constant. Each operation gate, including a unary gate, costs one.

The circuit computes \(F_n\) exactly if its ordered output vector equals \(F_n(x)\) for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\). The number \(\operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(F_n)\) is the minimum gate count of any such circuit. Competing circuits are nonuniform: the choice at each length is independent, and no algorithm is required to construct their descriptions. In contrast, the polynomial-time algorithm for \(F\) must work uniformly at all lengths. This distinction is part of the target.

The statement \(\operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(F_n)=O(n)\) means that there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(n_0\ge1\) such that \(\operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(F_n)\le Cn\) for every integer \(n\ge n_0\). The displayed target is its exact negation. It does not require \(\operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(F_n)/n\) to tend to infinity at every sufficiently large length. The function, its program and its running-time polynomial are chosen before all the lower-bound quantifiers.

The source uses AND, OR and NOT gates and leaves “explicit” broad. Every full-basis gate has a constant-size AND/OR/NOT implementation, and those gates are already allowed in \(B_2\). Thus changing between these two fixed bases changes minimum size by at most a constant factor and preserves the not-\(O(n)\) target. The polynomial-time explicitness convention is the previously recorded specialization of the source; it is not claimed to be equivalent to every possible meaning of “explicit.” No linearity or other algebraic restriction is imposed on \(F\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated existence claim. A positive answer must specify one total length-preserving function, prove that one uniform deterministic algorithm computes it in polynomial time, and prove the displayed lower bound against every circuit in the full model. A negative answer must show that every such polynomial-time function has \(O(n)\)-size nonuniform circuits, allowing the constant and starting length to depend on the function. A fixed constant-factor lower bound does not establish the target. Nor does a lower bound only for formulas, monotone circuits, XOR-only circuits or a fixed depth bound without a proof extending it to unrestricted circuits. The claim is unconditional, and an oracle-relative or conditional separation alone does not settle it. All complexity and quantifier requirements are exact; no numerical acceptance tolerance applies.

title: L versus NL
summary: Directed reachability asks whether a path follows the arrows from a specified source to a target. Nondeterministic logarithmic space can recognize it, and the problem captures the whole class NL. The target is one always-correct deterministic algorithm with only logarithmic writable memory on every explicit input. Savitch’s larger-space simulation and Reingold’s undirected algorithm do not settle this directed logarithmic-space target. A solution requires either a uniform algorithm with all resource guarantees or a lower bound excluding every eligible deterministic decider.
formal:
Is \(\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{NL}\)? Equivalently, do there exist a single deterministic Turing machine \(A\) and a constant \(C\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), directed graph \(G\) on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and \(s,t\in[n]\), the machine halts, correctly decides whether \(t\) is reachable from \(s\), and visits at most
\[C\left\lceil\log_2(n+2)\right\rceil\]
work-tape cells? The graph is given explicitly by its adjacency matrix; the input is read-only. The machine and constant must work for all input sizes.
definitions:
A directed graph has a set \(E\subseteq[n]\times[n]\) of ordered edges. Self-loops are allowed. Reachability asks whether there are vertices \(v_0=s,\ldots,v_\ell=t\), with \(\ell\ge0\), such that \((v_{i-1},v_i)\in E\) for every \(1\le i\le\ell\). In particular \(s=t\) is a yes instance. No degree, planarity, acyclicity or unique-path restriction is imposed.

The input contains a self-delimiting binary encoding of \(n\), all \(n^2\) adjacency bits in row order, and \(s,t\) in fixed-length binary vertex fields. Its bit length is \(N=\Theta(n^2)\), so logarithmic bounds in \(N+2\) and \(n+2\) agree up to constants. Malformed strings, including invalid dimensions and vertex fields, are rejected with logarithmic workspace in their actual length. A validity check does not need to store the matrix. The representation is an explicit string, not an adjacency oracle or a circuit describing a much larger graph.

The computation uses a fixed finite program, a read-only input tape bounded by endmarkers, and a fixed number of initially blank read/write work tapes over fixed finite alphabets. Heads move by ordinary Turing-machine steps. Space is the total number of distinct work-tape cells visited during the computation, including blank cells crossed by heads, all counters, stacks and auxiliary records. The finite control and read-only input cells are uncharged. There is no advice depending on input size, oracle, random tape, external storage, writable input or extra tape whose contents can temporarily be borrowed. The output is a single accept/reject decision. Input rescanning and arbitrary finite computation are permitted, but every input must eventually halt.

Use [L and NL](definitions.html#space) with the read-only input and work-space convention above. A nondeterministic branch may be clocked in polynomial time because the number of logspace configurations is polynomial.

Directed reachability is NL-complete under deterministic logarithmic-space many-one reductions. Such a reduction writes one polynomial-length instance and preserves its yes/no answer while using logarithmic workspace; output bits can be recomputed when composing it with another small-space machine. Thus a positive answer for the specified matrix representation implies \(\mathrm{NL}\subseteq\mathrm{L}\), and \(\mathrm{L}\subseteq\mathrm{NL}\) already holds.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of \(\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{NL}\), using the stated uniform machine model. An affirmative reachability solution must specify one machine and a constant, and prove correctness, termination, malformed-input handling and the space bound on every input. A negative solution must exclude every such machine: equivalently, for every always-halting correct deterministic reachability decider and every constant \(C\), some valid instance exceeds \(C\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) visited work cells. A class-based argument must establish the equivalence to this concrete reachability target. A lower bound for one search procedure, or a successful algorithm restricted to undirected graphs, using advice, nondeterminism or a higher power of logarithmic space, is insufficient. No numerical approximation of a resource bound answers this exact class-equality question.

title: Minimum Circuit Size Problem
summary: The Minimum Circuit Size Problem asks whether a complete Boolean truth table can be computed by a circuit below a given size threshold. The card fixes AND, OR and NOT gates, counts all gates, and measures input length by the full truth table. The target is NP-completeness under uniform deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. Known results for restricted proof systems, conditional quasipolynomial reductions and implicit representations do not settle that target. A complete answer must prove or refute the existence of a SAT reduction with exactly these guarantees.
formal:
Is the Minimum Circuit Size Problem (MCSP), with a complete truth table as input, NP-complete under uniform deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? Equivalently, does there exist one deterministic polynomial-time function \(g\) such that
\[\forall x\in\{0,1\}^{*},\qquad x\in\mathrm{SAT}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ g(x)\in\mathrm{MCSP}?\]
Use the exact circuit model and language below. The target is unconditional and unrelativized. A reduction may not use random bits, advice, an oracle, a gap promise, a partial truth table or an implicitly represented truth table.
definitions:
Use the [Boolean circuit convention](definitions.html#boolean-circuits) \(\mathrm{DM}\): binary AND/OR and unary NOT, with one output and free input wires, constant sources and wires. Every operation gate, including NOT, counts. The minimum size is \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\). This is the source's total-gate \(R\) measure; it is not a binary-gate-only measure or the full \(B_2\) basis. Exact thresholds below use this convention.

The truth table \(t\in\{0,1\}^{N}\), where \(N=2^n\), lists the values of a total function \(f_t:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\) in lexicographic input order. A well-formed instance is \((t,s)\), with integer \(0\le s\le N\) written in binary. It is a yes-instance exactly when \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f_t)\le s\). To fix a binary language, encode a pair as \(1^{|t|}0t\operatorname{bin}(s)\), with no leading zeros in \(\operatorname{bin}(s)\), except that zero is encoded as the single bit 0. Strings failing this syntax, the power-of-two length requirement, \(n\ge1\), or the threshold bound are no-instances. The input length is \(2N+1+O(\log(N+1))\), so polynomial time is measured in the full truth-table length, not merely in the number \(n\) of variables. The redundant unary length prefix is only a fixed efficiently decodable pair encoding.

Constants have been made explicit to remove a convention left implicit in the source. For a nonconstant function, constant inputs can be eliminated gate by gate without increasing size, so allowing them does not change its optimum. For the two constant functions the answer follows directly from the specified convention. No claim that all Boolean bases preserve exact optimum sizes is needed.

Use the shared definitions of [polynomial-time many-one reductions](definitions.html#reductions) and [SAT](definitions.html#sat), with uniform deterministic bit computation and one explicitly written target instance. SAT uses a fixed ordinary explicit binary formula encoding, with malformed inputs rejected. Polynomially interconvertible ordinary formula encodings preserve this reduction question.

Use [NP](definitions.html#p-np) and [NP-hardness and completeness](definitions.html#reductions) in their shared senses. MCSP is in NP: a circuit with at most \(s\le N\) gates has an explicit topologically ordered description of \(O(N\log(N+1))\) bits, and evaluating it on all \(N\) assignments checks the entire table in polynomial time. Thus the displayed SAT reduction suffices, by SAT's NP-completeness, and its nonexistence would refute NP-completeness under this reduction convention.

For context only, use the shared definitions of [P](definitions.html#p-np) and [BPP](definitions.html#randomization). The source also asks whether MCSP might lie in BPP. That is a separate proposition, not the logical negation of NP-hardness: the two possibilities are not an unconditional exhaustive or disjoint classification.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the existence of the displayed SAT-to-MCSP reduction. A positive answer must specify a uniform deterministic reduction, prove its polynomial running time and output length, and prove the yes/no equivalence for every input using the exact total truth-table and gate-count conventions above. A negative answer must prove that every deterministic polynomial-time candidate reduction fails on some input. A conditional theorem, an oracle-relative theorem, hardness under randomized or quasipolynomial-time reductions, a lower bound for a restricted proof system, or hardness of a partial, implicit or gap variant does not alone meet this criterion. No additive numerical tolerance applies to this exact language-reduction statement.

title: P versus PSPACE
summary: Polynomial space permits a computation to reuse its memory while exploring potentially enormous collections of possibilities. The question asks whether every problem solvable with that memory budget is also solvable in polynomial time. Truth of quantified Boolean formulas supplies a concrete complete problem. Alternating existential and universal choices describe strategies that can be much larger than one ordinary certificate. The project tests whether repeated reuse of a modest workspace gives strictly more decision power than any polynomial-time computation.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\)? Equivalently, can a single deterministic Turing machine decide the truth of every fully quantified Boolean formula in \(C(N+1)^k\) steps for fixed \(C,k\ge1\), where \(N\) is its encoded bit length?
definitions: Use [P](definitions.html#p-np), [PSPACE](definitions.html#space) and [TQBF](definitions.html#polynomial-hierarchy). Each well-formed input gives an explicit quantifier prefix on distinct Boolean variables followed by an AND/OR/NOT formula whose variables are all bound. Its full binary encoding, including variable identifiers, counts toward \(N\). Reject malformed inputs. The number of quantifiers and alternations may grow with the instance.
answer_criterion: Prove \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\) or \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{PSPACE}\). The first outcome asserts a deterministic polynomial-time decision procedure for every polynomial-space language; the second asserts a polynomial-space language with no deterministic polynomial-time decision procedure.

title: NP versus P/poly
summary: A nonuniform Boolean circuit family may choose a completely different circuit for each input length without any computable construction rule. The question asks whether one fixed language in NP nevertheless exceeds every polynomial bound on the number of Boolean gates. The card specifies the verifier model, exact circuit evaluation and the required arbitrarily large violating lengths. Counting arguments produce hard truth tables but do not by themselves supply the required polynomially verifiable language. Karp–Lipton, natural proofs and newer restricted-circuit lower bounds explain the surrounding landscape while leaving the full NP versus P/poly target unresolved.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{NP}\nsubseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\)? More explicitly, does there exist one language \(L\in\mathrm{NP}\) such that \[\forall C,k,n_0\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\ \exists n\geq n_0:\quad\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(L_n)>C(n+1)^k,\] where \(n\) is an integer, \(L_n\) is the characteristic function of \(L\) on \(n\)-bit strings and \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}\) is minimum Boolean circuit size in the model below?
definitions:
Use the shared definitions of [NP and the characteristic functions \(L_n\)](definitions.html#p-np), [P/poly](definitions.html#advice), and [Boolean circuits](definitions.html#boolean-circuits). The minimum size is \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(L_n)\): binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates count, while constants, inputs and wires are free. Circuits compute every \(n\)-bit membership value exactly and may be chosen independently at each length, including \(n=0\).

The NP verifier is one uniform deterministic polynomial-time bit algorithm with polynomial-length witnesses. Use an explicit pair encoding such as \(1^{|x|}0xy\); malformed pair encodings are rejected. The verifier and bounds are fixed for the language, and the verifier halts on all pairs. The circuit family has no uniform generation requirement.

The language \(L\) is chosen before the universal quantifiers over circuit bounds. It cannot change with \(k\), \(C\) or \(n_0\). Exceeding each bound at arbitrarily large lengths suffices; the conjecture does not demand exceeding it at every sufficiently large length. Conversely, if a polynomial bound holds except at finitely many lengths, enlarging its constant covers those lengths too, so this formulation is exactly noncontainment in \(\mathrm{P/poly}\).
answer_criterion: Provide a complete Lean-verified proof of the noncontainment proposition or of its negation \(\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\). A separation must supply one NP language that escapes every polynomial circuit-size bound with the quantifier order stated above. Different languages for different exponents are insufficient. To establish containment, prove that every NP language has a polynomial-size nonuniform family; equivalently, polynomial-size circuits for one NP-complete language such as SAT at all input lengths suffice. No efficient or computable circuit generator is required. Lower bounds for circuits with extra depth or gate restrictions, or for a language only known to lie in a larger class than NP, do not alone settle the target.

title: Strictness of the polynomial hierarchy
summary: The polynomial hierarchy classifies decision languages by a fixed number of alternating existential and universal blocks. Each block chooses polynomially many bits, followed by a uniform polynomial-time check. The question asks whether every added block strictly increases the class of expressible languages. Equality of any neighboring levels would make the entire hierarchy stabilize at a finite level. Known oracle separations and conditional collapses reveal consequences and barriers while leaving this unrelativized conjecture unresolved.
formal: For every integer \(k\ge0\), is \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm{P}}\subsetneq\Sigma_{k+1}^{\mathrm{P}}\)? In other words, must each additional fixed block of polynomially bounded alternating Boolean quantifiers enable a decision language that cannot be expressed with k blocks? The classes are the uniform, unrelativized classes defined below.
definitions:
Use the [polynomial hierarchy](definitions.html#polynomial-hierarchy) with \(k\) fixed for the whole language. Each block chooses a string of exactly \(p(|x|)=a(|x|+1)^b\) bits for fixed integers \(a\ge1,b\ge0\). Unused witness bits may be ignored. Encode the predicate's tuple by concatenating \(1^{|s|}0s\) for each of its \(k+1\) components. The deterministic bit machine rejects malformed tuples and halts in time polynomial in their full encoded length.

The inclusion \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\subseteq\Sigma_{k+1}^{\mathrm P}\) holds by adding an unused block. Strictness asks for a language in the difference at each \(k\). That language may depend on \(k\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of strict containment for every nonnegative integer k, or prove that \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm{P}}=\Sigma_{k+1}^{\mathrm{P}}\) for some fixed nonnegative integer k. The negative answer is exactly the logical negation, since the inclusions are unconditional. Equality at one adjacent pair collapses all higher finite levels. A separation of finitely many initial levels, an oracle separation, or a collapse conditional on an unproved hypothesis is insufficient to settle the displayed all-level assertion. No concrete finite input is required as a witness to a class equality or separation.

title: NEXP versus coNEXP
summary: NEXP consists of languages accepted by a uniform nondeterministic machine in time exponential in a polynomial of the input length. coNEXP consists of the complements of those languages. The question is whether these two classes are equal. A complement machine may use a different fixed polynomial in its exponent, but it receives no advice or oracle. A complete Lean-checked proof of equality or unconditional separation is required.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{NEXP}=\mathrm{coNEXP}\)? In other words, for every \(L\in\mathrm{NEXP}\), does its complement in \(\{0,1\}^{*}\) also have a nondeterministic exponential-time decider?
definitions:
Use the uniform [exponential-time classes](definitions.html#exponential-time). Here \(N=|x|\) includes the empty-string case. The machine has fixed finite alphabets and tapes, with at most two possible transitions per step. Every branch halts within \(C\,2^{(N+1)^k}\) transitions. One accepting branch suffices.

For each language \(L\), the proposed complement machine and its constants may depend on \(L\). That one machine must recognize \(\{0,1\}^{*}\setminus L\) at every input length. The statement imposes no effective compiler from a machine for \(L\) to one for its complement.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of \(\mathrm{NEXP}=\mathrm{coNEXP}\), or of its logical negation. A proof of equality must establish complement closure with exactly the model and quantifiers above. A proof of inequality must establish the existence of a language \(L\in\mathrm{NEXP}\) whose complement lies outside \(\mathrm{NEXP}\), excluding every uniform nondeterministic exponential-time bound for that complement.

A conditional separation, a result with an oracle or length-dependent advice, a lower bound only against a fixed exponent, or consistency of a separation with a selected formal theory does not settle the unconditional class equality. This is a yes-or-no class-comparison question, with no numerical approximation target.

title: Polynomial-size circuits for EXP
summary: EXP contains problems solvable in deterministic exponential time. The question asks whether every such problem could nevertheless have polynomial-size Boolean circuits chosen separately for each input length. The circuits need not be efficiently constructible, making this different from a polynomial-time simulation. Time hierarchy theorems alone do not eliminate that nonuniform possibility. The project seeks a lower bound strong enough to defeat arbitrary length-specific circuit designs for some language with an explicit exponential-time decision procedure.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\)? More explicitly, does there exist a language \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\), decidable by one deterministic exponential-time algorithm, whose circuit complexity \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(L_n)\) satisfies \[\forall C\geq1\;\forall k\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}\;\forall n_0\geq1\;\exists n\geq n_0:\quad \operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(L_n)>C(n+1)^{k}?\]
definitions:
Use the shared definitions of [EXP](definitions.html#exponential-time), [P/poly](definitions.html#advice) and [Boolean circuits](definitions.html#boolean-circuits). Write \(L_n\) for the characteristic function of \(L\) on \(n\)-bit strings and \(\operatorname{CC}_{\mathrm{DM}}(L_n)\) for its minimum exact circuit size. Binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates count; inputs, constants and wires are free. This specifies the former “noninput gates” convention: charging the two available constants would change size by at most two and leave this polynomial-size question unchanged.

The EXP algorithm is one uniform deterministic multitape Turing machine, with no promise, advice or oracle. The circuits are nonuniform; their choices at different lengths need not be computable. One language must defeat every polynomial size bound, at arbitrarily large lengths for each bound. No eventually-everywhere superpolynomial lower bound is required.

The source uses exponential-time notation in a truth-table generation discussion; this card uses the standard union defining EXP. Replacing EXP by \(\mathrm E=\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{O(n)})\) gives an equivalent class-containment question by polynomial padding.
answer_criterion: Provide a complete Lean-checked proof of \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\), including an EXP language and the quantified superpolynomial lower bound, or prove its negation \(\mathrm{EXP}\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\). Different hard languages for different fixed exponents, a lower bound for a restricted gate basis, or a consistency theorem alone do not settle the question.

title: L versus P
summary: Logarithmic-space computation can retain only a few input indices and counters while repeatedly rereading the input. The question asks whether that memory always suffices for every polynomial-time decision problem. Evaluating a supplied Boolean circuit is a representative complete task. Shared dependencies make naive recomputation expensive, while storing all intermediate gate values exceeds the space budget. The project tests whether efficient computation fundamentally needs substantial working memory or can always reorganize its information into an extremely small state.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{P}\)? Equivalently, can a deterministic algorithm decide Circuit Value using \(O(\log(N+2))\) work space on every input of \(N\) bits?
definitions: Use the uniform [logspace](definitions.html#space) and [polynomial-time](definitions.html#p-np) conventions. Circuit Value supplies a [Boolean circuit](definitions.html#boolean-circuits) in topological order, Boolean values for its inputs and one designated output. Its AND, OR and NOT gates may have unrestricted circuit depth. The instance gives the whole DAG and input assignment, totaling \(N\) bits. Accept when the output is one, and reject malformed inputs. The machine can revisit its read-only input, has only ordinary initially blank work tapes, and must halt on every input.
answer_criterion: Prove \(\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{P}\) or \(\mathrm{L}\ne \mathrm{P}\) in the read-only-input model defined here. Equality means that every polynomial-time decision language admits a halting deterministic logarithmic-space machine; inequality means that at least one such language admits none.

title: Nonuniform \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) versus \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\)
summary: TC0 circuits use a constant number of layers of powerful majority gates. NC1 circuits use logarithmically many layers of ordinary bounded-input Boolean gates. The question asks whether the former nonuniform class is strictly weaker than the latter. Many arithmetic tasks already fit in TC0, so their familiar sequential implementations do not provide separating examples. The project seeks a function whose nested logical dependencies cannot be compressed into a fixed-depth network even when each gate can aggregate many inputs at once.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\subsetneq \mathrm{NC}^{1}\) for the nonuniform circuit classes defined below? Equivalently, does there exist a Boolean function family \(f=(f_{n}:\{0,1\}^{n}\to \{0,1\})\) in \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) such that for every fixed depth \(d\ge 1\), exponent \(k\ge 1\), and constant \(M\ge 1\), there is an n for which every depth-at-most-d majority circuit computing \(f_{n}\) exactly has size greater than \(M(n+1)^{k}\)?
definitions: Use a [Boolean circuit](definitions.html#boolean-circuits) with \(n\) input nodes, constants 0 and 1 available, and one designated output. Depth is the maximum number of gates on an input-to-output path. Size is the number of gates plus the number of wires; if an input is repeated at a gate, each occurrence counts as a wire. A majority circuit has AND and OR gates of arbitrary positive fan-in, NOT gates of fan-in one, and MAJ gates of arbitrary positive fan-in m, with output 1 exactly when strictly more than \(m/2\) inputs equal one. An even tie gives zero. \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) consists of all families with such circuits of size at most \(M(n+1)^k\) and depth at most d for every n, for some constants M,k,d depending on the family. \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) consists of families with circuits over AND, OR, NOT, with fan-in at most two (one for NOT), size at most \(M(n+1)^k\), and depth at most \(b \log _{2}(n+1)\), for fixed M,k,b. Circuits may share intermediate gates. Both classes are nonuniform: an arbitrary separate circuit may be chosen for each input length, without any requirement to compute its description. The output must be correct on every input; no randomness, approximation, promise, or distributional error is allowed.
answer_criterion: Prove \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\subsetneq \mathrm{NC}^{1}\) or \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}=\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) for the nonuniform families defined here. Strictness requires a single \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) family with no polynomial-size constant-depth majority-circuit family; equality requires that every \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) family admit such a family.

title: NEXP versus nonuniform \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\)
summary: Does some NEXP language escape all polynomial-size constant-depth majority circuits? Majority gates make this circuit class substantially more powerful than constant-depth \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}\) circuits. Williams established the corresponding separation for ACC circuits with fixed-modulus gates. Recent threshold-circuit bounds still restrict depth or polynomial size and use different hard-language classes. The target requires one ordinary NEXP language outside the entire nonuniform class \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\).
formal: Is there a language \(L\in\mathrm{NEXP}\) outside nonuniform \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\)? Such an \(L\) must satisfy the following for all integers \(d,k,C,n_0\ge1\): some \(n\ge n_0\) has no circuit of depth at most \(d\) and size at most \(C(n+1)^k\) over AND, OR, NOT and majority that computes \(L_n\) on all \(n\)-bit inputs.
definitions: Use uniform [NEXP](definitions.html#exponential-time). Use a [Boolean circuit](definitions.html#boolean-circuits) with \(n\) input nodes, constants 0 and 1 available, and one designated output. AND and OR may have any positive fan-in; NOT has one input. A majority gate on m inputs outputs 1 when at least \(\lceil m/2\rceil\) of them are 1, including a tie when m is even. Fan-out is unrestricted. Size is the number of operation gates plus wires. Repeated connections count individually, so their multiplicities cannot encode uncharged weights. Depth is the maximum number of operation gates on an input-to-output path. All circuits compute exactly on every input; no average-case correctness or randomness is allowed. \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) consists of languages having one fixed depth bound and one polynomial size bound across all input lengths. The family may be nonuniform: no algorithm is required to construct its nth circuit. NEXP machines are uniform and have no oracle or advice. The formal quantifiers permit the lower bound to be witnessed at infinitely many input lengths, rather than requiring failure at every sufficiently large length.
answer_criterion: A positive resolution proves that one language in NEXP has no polynomial-size constant-depth majority-circuit family, with depth and polynomial exponent both unrestricted constants. A negative resolution proves \(\mathrm{NEXP}\subseteq \mathrm{TC}^{0}\). A bound ruling out only \(n^{k}\) gates for one fixed k, or only one fixed circuit depth, does not by itself establish the displayed separation.

title: Exponential circuit lower bounds for 3-SAT
summary: The question asks whether n-variable 3-SAT requires Boolean circuits of size at least two to a positive constant times n at every sufficiently large n. Inputs are complete incidence vectors for all clauses of width at most three, giving Theta(n cubed) input bits. The circuit model permits every two-input Boolean gate, arbitrary sharing and independent nonuniform designs at each length. Known restricted-circuit lower bounds and randomized exponential-time improvements do not settle this unrestricted lower-bound target. A complete answer must prove the eventual exponential bound or its exact quantified negation in Lean.
formal:
For the explicitly encoded \(n\)-variable 3-SAT function \(\mathrm{SAT}_n\) below, do there exist constants \(c>0\) and integer \(n_0\ge1\) such that
\[\forall n\ge n_0,\qquad \operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(\mathrm{SAT}_n)\ge 2^{cn}?\]
The circuit lower bound is against arbitrary nonuniform Boolean circuits of fan-in at most two. Its exponential parameter is the number \(n\) of variables, not the number of input bits in the clause-incidence encoding. The card retains this previously recorded variable-parameter specialization of the source’s exponential-SAT conjecture.
definitions:
Fix an integer \(n\ge1\) and variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). A clause is a disjunction of zero, one, two or three literals on distinct variables. Each literal is either \(x_i\) or \(\neg x_i\). The empty clause is false. Clauses never contain both signs of one variable or repeated variables. The list contains
\[M(n)=\sum_{j=0}^{3}2^{j}\binom{n}{j}\]
clauses, with \(\binom{n}{j}=0\) when \(j>n\). Order them first by their length, then lexicographically by their increasing tuple of variable indices, then lexicographically by their sign bits, with 0 meaning positive and 1 negated.

An input is a bit vector \(b\in\{0,1\}^{M(n)}\). Its \(i\)-th bit specifies whether clause \(i\) is included. Let \(\Phi_b\) be the conjunction of exactly those included clauses; the empty conjunction is true. Define
\[\mathrm{SAT}_n(b)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists a\in\{0,1\}^{n}\text{ satisfying }\Phi_b.\]
Every input vector is valid. Formulas are specified in full, not by a circuit or oracle that answers clause queries. All assignments are permitted; there is no uniqueness, sparsity or satisfiability promise. This representation includes clauses of width at most three. In ordinary lists, repeated literals can be removed, tautological clauses discarded and duplicate clauses merged without changing satisfiability.

Use the [Boolean circuit convention](definitions.html#boolean-circuits) with the full \(B_2\) basis and free constants. A competing circuit has \(M(n)\) input bits and one output, and must compute \(\mathrm{SAT}_n\) exactly on every clause-incidence vector. Its minimum size is \(\operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(\mathrm{SAT}_n)\). The circuit choice for each \(n\) is arbitrary; no uniform generator is required. Here the encoded input length is \(N=M(n)\), while the exponential lower-bound parameter is the variable count \(n\).

The circuit has \(M(n)=\Theta(n^3)\) inputs, so the conjectured size is \(2^{\Omega(n)}=2^{\Omega(M(n)^{1/3})}\). A claim exponential in the raw input length would be a different target and is not asserted. Switching between \(B_2\) and the bounded-fan-in AND/OR/NOT basis changes size by at most a fixed constant factor, preserving the existence of a positive exponential lower-bound exponent after adjusting constants.

The quantifiers are almost everywhere in the variable count: one positive exponent \(c\) must work at every sufficiently large \(n\). Their exact negation is
\[\forall c>0\ \forall N\ge1\ \exists n\ge N:\quad \operatorname{CC}_{B_2}(\mathrm{SAT}_n)<2^{cn}.\]
The integers \(n_0,N,n\) and real \(c\) have the domains just stated. A size bound \(2^{o(n)}\) at all lengths would imply the negative answer, but is stronger than this negation, which permits different favorable lengths for different exponents.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed eventual exponential circuit lower bound for the exact total function family defined here. A positive answer must establish one fixed \(c>0\) and threshold \(n_0\), and prove the lower bound against every correct circuit at every \(n\ge n_0\). A negative answer must establish the quantified negation stated above. Lower bounds only for formulas, monotone circuits, bounded depth, uniform algorithms or restricted proof systems do not meet the criterion. A uniform exponential-time upper bound with a fixed positive exponent remains compatible with a smaller positive lower-bound exponent. Neither a conditional theorem nor an oracle-relative theorem alone resolves this unconditional target. Asymptotic quantifiers are exact; numerical acceptance tolerance is not applied to exponents or big-O notation.

title: KRW formula-size conjecture with constant loss
summary: The selected KRW variant asks whether minimum formula size under block composition is always within a constant factor of the product of the two minimum sizes. Both functions can be arbitrary nonconstant Boolean functions, and the inner one is applied to disjoint input blocks. Formulas use binary AND and OR with negation, count variable occurrences, and cannot share intermediate computations. The constant must work for every function and dimension, so dimension-dependent losses do not suffice. The original depth conjecture and recent results for strengthened communication tasks are related but distinct statements.
formal:
Is there an absolute constant \(\alpha>0\) such that for every pair of positive integers \(n,m\) and every pair of nonconstant total Boolean functions \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\), \(g:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}\),
\[\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(g\circ f)\ge\alpha \operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(g)\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)?\]
Here \((g\circ f)(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(m)})=g(f(x^{(1)}),\ldots,f(x^{(m)}))\) on \(m\) disjoint \(n\)-bit blocks, and \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}\) is minimum De Morgan formula leaf size. The constant is chosen before all dimensions and functions.

This card retains the constant-factor formula-size version displayed as Conjecture 5.13 in the source book. It is stronger than versions permitting a growing multiplicative loss. The original KRW paper formulates a depth-composition question; the card does not identify that question, weakened quantitative versions, and the displayed constant-loss formula statement as equivalent.
definitions:
For a positive integer \(r\), a total Boolean function is \(h:\{0,1\}^r\to\{0,1\}\). Nonconstant means that it takes both values, not that it depends on every input. Use [De Morgan formula leaf size](definitions.html#formula-size), denoted \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(h)\). Formulas are trees of binary AND/OR and unary NOT, with no shared internal values, and must agree with \(h\) on every input. This is a positive finite minimum for a nonconstant function. There is no randomness, promise, threshold gate or unbounded fan-in.

The composed function has exactly \(mn\) designated coordinates \(x^{(j)}_i\), with \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Block coordinates are distinct and unconstrained. The same inner function \(f\) is applied to every block, and its outputs, in block order, become the inputs of \(g\). The composition symbol here means this block operation, not ordinary composition of two maps with the same domain. Both functions and their composition may be specified by arbitrary finite truth tables, and no uniformity, polynomial-time evaluability, or monotonicity is assumed.

Since both functions are nonconstant, every Boolean vector supplied to \(g\) can be realized by some collection of blocks, and the composition is nonconstant. The usual substitution bound gives \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(g\circ f)\le \operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(g)\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(f)\). The question is whether the ratio to that upper bound is bounded away from zero uniformly over all functions and dimensions. Equivalently, is the infimum of these positive ratios strictly positive? This infimum need not be attained. Restricting \(0<\alpha\le1\) is equivalent.

The negation says that for every positive \(\alpha\), some pair and dimensions have ratio smaller than \(\alpha\). Thus a single saving relative to exact multiplication, or even failure of one proposed constant, is insufficient to refute the claim. Allowing constant functions with the convention \(\operatorname{FS}_{\mathrm{DM}}(h)=0\) would add only trivial inequalities; their exclusion makes the ratio formulation well-defined. Minimum depth, which counts gates along a longest path, is a different measure from the number of leaves.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the constant-loss formula-size statement. A positive answer must establish one strictly positive factor for every permitted pair and dimensions. A negative answer must establish ratios arbitrarily close to zero, not merely a finite violation of equality or an unbounded additive saving in formula depth. Bounds for almost all functions, for special inner functions, for monotone formulas, or for a stronger communication search task do not alone prove the all-function claim. A composition inequality with a loss depending on either dimension, even polylogarithmically, is a weaker result unless upgraded to the fixed constant required here.

title: Majority outside constant-depth modular circuits
summary: Majority returns one when at least half of its input bits are one. ACC⁰ circuits combine Boolean operations and modular-counting gates using constant depth and polynomial size. The question asks whether every fixed choice of modulus and depth fails to compute majority within polynomial size. Known results for prime moduli or additional circuit restrictions do not settle the full composite-modulus question. A separation would show that this shallow modular model cannot express a basic threshold operation efficiently.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{MAJ}\notin\mathrm{ACC}^{0}\)? Precisely, for every fixed modulus \(m\geq2\), depth bound \(d\geq1\), constants \(C\geq1\), \(k\geq1\), and \(N\geq1\), is there an input length \(n\geq N\) for which no depth-at-most-\(d\) circuit over AND, OR, NOT and \(\mathrm{MOD}_{m}\), with at most \(C(n+1)^k\) gates, computes \(\mathrm{MAJ}_{n}\) exactly?
definitions: For \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), \(\mathrm{MAJ}_{n}(x)=1\) if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\geq\lceil n/2\rceil\). An ACC circuit is a finite acyclic Boolean circuit with one output, unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and \(\mathrm{MOD}_m\) gates, fan-in-one NOT gates, and constants. A \(\mathrm{MOD}_{m}\) gate outputs one precisely when the sum of its Boolean inputs is divisible by \(m\). Depth is the maximum number of noninput gates on an input-output path, including NOT gates. Size is the number of noninput gates; counting wires instead gives the same polynomial-size class. The modulus, depth and polynomial-size constants are fixed for the whole family and cannot depend on \(n\). Circuits may be chosen separately for every length, without any construction algorithm, uniformity or bound on fan-out. The class \(\mathrm{ACC}^{0}\) is the union of these polynomial-size, constant-depth families over all fixed moduli. Allowing a fixed finite collection of moduli is equivalent, by using their common multiple with a constant-size gate substitution. All assignments must be computed correctly; no probability of error is allowed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the universal lower-bound statement, or refute it by proving the existence of fixed \(m,d,C,k\) and circuits of size at most \(C(n+1)^k\) computing majority for every input length. Refuting one fixed size exponent is insufficient for a positive answer. Results for a prime modulus, a restricted wiring symmetry, uniform circuits alone or a different hard function do not meet the complete criterion.

title: Berman–Hartmanis conjecture
summary: Polynomial-time reductions show that NP-complete problems can simulate each other, but may erase information. The Berman-Hartmanis conjecture asks whether every pair instead admits a polynomial-time computable bijection with a polynomial-time inverse. That bijection must preserve yes and no instances across the entire string space. Padding provides evidence for familiar complete problems without covering all possible complete languages. The project asks whether completeness forces one efficiently reversible organization of instances, reaching beyond ordinary mutual reducibility.
formal: For every pair of NP-complete languages \(A,B\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\), is there a bijection \(f:\{0,1\}^{*}\to\{0,1\}^{*}\) such that both \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\) are computable in deterministic polynomial time and \(x\in A\iff f(x)\in B\) for every binary string \(x\)?
definitions: Take [NP](definitions.html#p-np) and completeness under [deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions](definitions.html#reductions). Membership in \(A\) and \(B\) is defined on all binary strings. The forward and inverse algorithms can depend on the pair \(A,B\). Each runs in polynomial time in its own input length, and the bijection may change lengths. The assertion is unconditional.
answer_criterion: Prove that every pair of polynomial-time many-one NP-complete languages is polynomial-time isomorphic, or prove that some pair has no bijection with both directions computable in polynomial time. The statement is unconditional: \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{NP}\) is not an added hypothesis.

title: Directed reachability in polynomial time and polylogarithmic space
summary: The problem asks for directed reachability to be decided simultaneously in polynomial time and polylogarithmic space. One uniform deterministic machine must meet both bounds on every explicitly encoded graph and marked vertex pair. No graph restrictions, randomness, advice or additional catalytic memory are allowed. Separate efficient-time and small-space algorithms do not satisfy the joint requirement. The target is equivalently inclusion of nondeterministic logspace in SC, and is weaker than L equaling NL.
formal:
Is there one deterministic algorithm that decides directed reachability using polynomial time and polylogarithmic working space simultaneously?

Precisely, does there exist a uniform deterministic Turing decider \(M\) and fixed positive integers \(a,k,c\) such that, for every encoded instance \((G,s,t)\) of bit length \(N\), it correctly decides whether \(t\) is reachable from \(s\), while
\[\operatorname{time}_M(G,s,t)\le c(N+2)^a\qquad\text{and}\qquad\operatorname{space}_M(G,s,t)\le c\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil^k?\]
Both bounds must hold for the same computation on every input. This is the question whether directed reachability belongs to the class SC.
definitions:
For an integer \(v\ge1\), the directed graph \(G=([v],E)\) has \([v]=\{1,\ldots,v\}\) and \(E\subseteq[v]\times[v]\). Loops are allowed, and repeated edges have no separate meaning. The graph may have cycles, arbitrary in- and out-degree and arbitrarily many paths. No planarity, acyclicity, uniqueness, few-path or connectivity promise is imposed. The marked vertices satisfy \(s,t\in[v]\).

Reachability means that for some integer \(\ell\ge0\) there are vertices \(u_0,\ldots,u_\ell\) with \(u_0=s\), \(u_\ell=t\) and \((u_i,u_{i+1})\in E\) for every \(i<\ell\). The zero-edge path makes every vertex reachable from itself. Whenever reachability holds, a path with at most \(v-1\) edges also exists. The required output is one membership bit; a path itself need not be output.

Use the explicit binary encoding \(1^v0\), followed by the \(v^2\) adjacency-matrix bits in row-major order, followed by fixed-width binary encodings of \(s,t\). Each vertex field has \(b_v=\lceil\log_2(v+1)\rceil\) bits and must represent an integer between \(1\) and \(v\). The total length is
\[N=v+1+v^2+2b_v.\]
There are no trailing fields. Any binary string failing this format is rejected. The machine must also meet the same time and space bounds on malformed inputs, measured by their actual length. This representation is polynomially related to the vertex count; it is not a succinct circuit description of an exponentially large graph.

The machine has one two-way read-only input tape and a fixed finite number of ordinary work tapes over fixed finite alphabets, initially blank. Each step changes the finite control, reads or writes a bounded number of tape symbols and moves each head by at most one cell. Time is the total number of steps until its accept/reject halt, in the worst case. Space is the maximum number of work-tape cells ever visited during the run, multiplied by a fixed number of bits sufficient to encode a tape symbol. In particular all counters, indices, remembered input bits and temporary data count toward space. Input storage and the finite control do not count. The single decision bit is the halting state, so no uncharged output tape can be used as working memory.

No random bits, nondeterministic choices, quantum register, oracle, advice, writable input or extra catalytic memory are available. The same finite program and constants work for all graph orders and all valid and malformed inputs. An algorithm may depend on the fixed encoding, but cannot be chosen separately for each graph. The input is read sequentially by its head rather than supplied as a unit-cost adjacency oracle; scanning it is charged to time.

For an ordinary language of binary strings, SC means decidability by a single uniform deterministic machine with a polynomial time bound and a fixed-power logarithmic space bound as above. It differs from merely supplying one polynomial-time algorithm and another polylogarithmic-space algorithm. The exponent \(k\) is allowed to be any fixed positive integer; the target does not specifically demand logarithmic or squared-logarithmic space.

Equivalently, the question is \(\mathrm{NL}\subseteq\mathrm{SC}\). Here NL consists of languages decided by a nondeterministic Turing machine with logarithmic charged work space and a fixed polynomial clock on every branch, accepting an input exactly when at least one branch accepts. Directed reachability is NL-complete under deterministic logarithmic-space many-one reductions, and those reductions preserve membership in SC. In particular, \(\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{NL}\) would imply an affirmative answer, but this card asks only for the weaker simultaneous bounds and does not assert the converse.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the simultaneous-bound existence statement. An affirmative answer must give one exact deterministic decider for all directed graphs and prove its polynomial time and fixed-power logarithmic space bounds with constants independent of the instance. A negative answer must prove that no such decider exists: for every correct uniform decider and every proposed constants, some input violates at least one bound. Separate algorithms meeting separate bounds, a restriction to a special graph family, or a simulation with randomness, advice or catalytic memory is insufficient.

title: Ruling out quasilinear-time SAT without a space restriction
summary: SAT asks whether an explicitly written Boolean formula has a satisfying assignment. The target excludes every deterministic running time n times a fixed polynomial in log n in a uniform random-access model. There is no independent restriction on working memory. Known small-space lower bounds and either/or resource alternatives do not establish this time-only statement. The formulation uses the quasilinear interpretation of the source’s informal near-linear goal.
formal:
Is Boolean-formula satisfiability outside deterministic quasilinear time, with no independent bound on the algorithm’s working memory? In the uniform random-access model below, the exact target is
\[\mathrm{SAT}\notin\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb N}\mathrm{DTIME}\!\left[N\left\lceil\log_2(N+2)\right\rceil^k\right],\]
where \(N\) is the full bit length of the explicitly written formula and \(\mathbb N\) includes zero. Thus every fixed polynomial-logarithmic factor must be excluded. The formulation uses this meaning of the source’s “near-linear time”; the stronger exclusion of all \(N^{1+o(1)}\)-time algorithms is not required.
definitions:
Use [SAT](definitions.html#sat) on fully written formula trees with Boolean constants. Each variable occurrence carries a binary identifier in \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and identifiers may be unused. The formula uses a self-delimiting prefix encoding with gate tokens and delimited identifiers. Every token and occurrence counts toward \(N\). Reject malformed strings.

Fix a uniform deterministic word-RAM with logarithmic-size words. A machine is one finite program independent of \(N\), together with a fixed integer \(b\ge1\) giving word length \(w_N=b\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil\). It has a fixed number of word registers and an initially zero writable memory array addressed by \(w_N\)-bit integers. The input is separately read-only, packed into words with zero padding in its final word, and its bit length is available. One step is a register copy, Boolean bitwise operation, addition or subtraction modulo \(2^{w_N}\), comparison, conditional branch, shift by a register-specified count, or indexed read/write of one word. Shifts by at least \(w_N\) return zero. Registers and memory words contain exactly \(w_N\) bits; no unbounded-integer operation has unit cost. The program has no advice, oracle, nondeterminism or random bits. It halts with a single accept/reject answer on every input. Standard additional arithmetic operations on logarithmic words can be implemented with polynomial-logarithmic overhead and do not change the union of time bounds in this question.

There is no logarithmic, sublinear or other independent workspace requirement. The algorithm may use any addressable working memory it can access during its allowed running time. Initial memory is zero, not an input-dependent precomputed table; reading and writing memory are charged. The word-size/address convention is the ordinary polynomial-address-space convention of this RAM model, not a small-space promise. In particular, maintaining an input-sized array is allowed. The purpose of random access is to charge actual computation rather than the distance a sequential input head must travel.

For a fixed \(k\), membership in the displayed time class means that some one machine and constant \(D\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) correctly decide every input \(x\) within
\[D(N+2)\left\lceil\log_2(N+2)\right\rceil^k\]
steps, including parsing and rejection of malformed inputs. Here \(k,D,b\) and the finite program are independent of the particular input and its length. The target’s positive statement excludes every such choice. Its negative statement requires just one correct algorithm and one fixed exponent \(k\); it does not require a linear-time algorithm.

The chosen bound is \(N\,\mathrm{polylog}(N)\), the union over all fixed logarithmic powers. It is smaller than the broader \(N^{1+o(1)}\) family: for example, \(N2^{\sqrt{\log_2 N}}\) is in the latter family but exceeds \(N(\log N)^k\) for every fixed \(k\). Excluding every \(N\,\mathrm{polylog}(N)\) algorithm does not require proving a fixed exponent lower bound \(N^{1+\varepsilon}\). The clarification retains the absence of a memory restriction and records which of these meanings is being benchmarked.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed time-only nonmembership statement for the stated uniform machine and input model. A positive answer must exclude all fixed \(k,D,b\) and all correct total programs, with no extra workspace restriction. Equivalently, for every correct total program, every \(k\), and every \(D\), some input exceeds its proposed quasilinear bound. A negative answer must provide one program and fixed constants and prove correctness and that time bound on all inputs. A lower bound only for logarithmic-memory algorithms, a restricted SAT-solver family, a particular input distribution, or a sequential-access model does not establish this RAM target. A conditional lower bound under P ≠ NP or an exponential-time hypothesis is not an unconditional solution. Exact asymptotic quantifiers apply; no finite timing experiment or numerical error tolerance settles the question.

title: PH versus PSPACE
summary: Does every polynomial-space decision problem lie in the polynomial hierarchy? PH allows a fixed number of alternating quantifier blocks for each language. PSPACE also describes polynomial-time alternation with no fixed bound on the number of alternations. Equality would put TQBF in one finite level and hence collapse PH to that level. Completeness and oracle results illuminate the distinction without settling the ordinary class equality.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{PH}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\)? Equivalently, does TQBF belong to \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm{P}}\) for some fixed \(k\ge0\)?
definitions: Use the [polynomial hierarchy and TQBF](definitions.html#polynomial-hierarchy) and [PSPACE](definitions.html#space). The input formula uses AND, OR and NOT. Its prefix binds each variable once and its entire binary encoding, including variable names, is available on a read-only tape. The number of input quantifier blocks can grow, while the proposed hierarchy level \(k\) is fixed for every input.
answer_criterion: A positive resolution proves \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\subseteq \mathrm{PH}\); the reverse inclusion is already known. Equivalently it places TQBF in one fixed \(\Sigma ^{p}_{k}\), which would put every PSPACE language in that same level by polynomial-time reductions. A negative resolution proves that some PSPACE language, equivalently TQBF, is outside every fixed level. A separation at one fixed level or an oracle-relative result alone does not answer the question.

title: Containment of PPAD in PLS
summary: PPAD captures directed parity search, while PLS captures search for a state whose proposed move does not improve a finite cost. The question asks whether every PPAD relation reduces to a PLS relation by uniform deterministic polynomial-time many-one search reductions. Equivalently, one must transform any End-of-Line instance into a Localopt instance and translate every Localopt solution back into an End-of-Line solution. The known identity CLS = PPAD ∩ PLS makes the proposed containment equivalent to CLS = PPAD. This asks for a relation between classes, independently of whether either class has polynomial-time solution algorithms.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{PPAD}\subseteq\mathrm{PLS}\) under uniform deterministic polynomial-time many-one search reductions? Here PPAD represents directed endpoint search and PLS represents potential-based local search, with precise definitions below. Equivalently, do there exist uniform deterministic polynomial-time computable maps \(F,G\) that transform every End-of-Line input \(I\) into a Localopt instance \(F(I)\), and transform every accepted Localopt answer \(w\) for that instance into an accepted End-of-Line answer \(G(I,w)\)? This asks only the displayed direction of containment.
definitions:
A Boolean circuit is given by an explicit topologically ordered list of gates over fan-in-two AND and OR, unary NOT, and constants 0 and 1, with listed input nodes and ordered output nodes. Counts, gate types, wire indices and delimiters use an unambiguous binary encoding. All lists are part of the input, rather than a program generating them; the numbers of input and output bits therefore contribute to the encoding length. The notation \(\{0,1\}^n\) denotes length-\(n\) bit strings, and \(0^n\) is the all-zero string.

Polynomial time means one uniform deterministic multitape Turing machine with a bound \(a(N+1)^d\), for fixed integers \(a,d\ge1\), on inputs of complete bit length \(N\). All bit operations and output bits count. Machines receive and may inspect full circuit gate lists; they have no advice, oracle or randomness unless randomness is explicitly allowed below. A malformed circuit encoding is efficiently recognizable. For a search task with such an input, INVALID is its only accepted answer, and INVALID is forbidden on valid inputs. Tags and bit strings in all answers have a fixed unambiguous binary encoding.

A total NP search problem is a relation \(R(x,y)\) on bit strings with a valid answer on every input \(x\), a fixed polynomial bound on the length of every accepted answer \(y\), and a deterministic polynomial-time test of \(R(x,y)\). TFNP denotes the class of these relations. A deterministic polynomial-time many-one search reduction from \(R\) to \(Q\) consists of maps \(F,G\) such that, for every \(x\) and every valid \(Q\)-answer \(z\) on \(F(x)\), the output \(G(x,z)\) is a valid \(R\)-answer on \(x\). Both maps are uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithms, with time measured in their full input bit lengths. Here FP means total search relations admitting a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that selects a valid answer, without requiring a unique answer.

An End-of-Line input consists of circuits \(S,P:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n\), for \(n\ge1\). The input is valid when \(P(0^n)=0^n\) and \(S(0^n)\ne0^n\), conditions checked by circuit evaluation. An answer is any \(v\in\{0,1\}^n\) with
\[P(S(v))\ne v\quad\text{or}\quad\bigl(v\ne0^n\ \text{and}\ S(P(v))\ne v\bigr).\]
Thus zero is accepted only for the first condition, not merely for being the designated start. Failed input conditions, like malformed encodings, have only the answer INVALID. No global inverse promise is imposed. The graph intuition uses an edge \(u\to v\) when \(u\ne v\), \(S(u)=v\) and \(P(v)=u\); the displayed answer relation is authoritative. Answers need not lie in the component of zero. The directed endpoint principle guarantees an answer. PPAD, short for Polynomial Parity Argument, Directed, is the subclass of TFNP reducible to this End-of-Line task by the many-one search reductions just defined.

A Localopt input consists of circuits \(T:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}^m\) and \(V:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}^r\), where \(m,r\ge1\). Read the output of \(V\) as an unsigned binary integer with the first output bit most significant. A valid answer is any \(w\in\{0,1\}^m\) satisfying
\[V(T(w))\ge V(w).\]
The circuit \(T\) proposes a next state and \(V\) assigns its cost; a solution is a state where that proposal does not improve the cost. A global minimum of \(V\) is always an accepted answer. There is no specified starting state or reachability restriction. Malformed encodings have only INVALID as an answer. Allowing distinct state and cost widths is polynomially equivalent by padding to the equal-width formulation in the cited source. PLS, short for Polynomial Local Search, is the subclass of TFNP reducible to Localopt by the specified many-one search reductions.

The required maps \(F,G\) are fixed for all circuit sizes. The output of \(F\) must be a well-formed Localopt instance even on a malformed End-of-Line encoding; such inputs can be sent to a fixed trivial instance, and \(G\) must then return INVALID. For every other input, correctness must hold for every accepted Localopt witness, not only for one chosen minimum or one reachable state. The time and output length of \(F\) are polynomial in \(|I|\); the time and output length of \(G\) are polynomial in \(|I|+|w|\). Consequently all output circuit sizes and the parameters \(m,r\) are polynomially bounded by \(|I|\). Neither map uses an oracle for solving either search task. This is one many-one reduction, not an adaptive sequence of calls. Since End-of-Line and Localopt are the defining complete tasks, existence of these maps is equivalent to the stated class containment.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that the specified maps F and G exist, including their polynomial bounds and correctness for every target answer, or prove that no such pair exists in the ordinary uniform model. A single hard-looking example, an oracle separation, a query lower bound or a conditional cryptographic claim is insufficient. A positive proof need not provide an efficient algorithm for solving Localopt. Establishing only the reverse containment does not answer this card.

title: P versus NP intersect coNP
summary: A language in NP intersect coNP has short efficiently checkable certificates for both yes and no instances. The question asks whether some such language still lies outside deterministic polynomial time. Having two kinds of witnesses does not automatically tell an algorithm how to find either one. The separation would identify difficulty independent of the asymmetric certification typical of NP-complete problems. The project explores whether efficiently verifiable certainty on both sides can coexist with an intrinsically hard decision process.
formal: Is \(\mathrm{P}\ne\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}\)? Equivalently, does there exist a language \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\) with polynomially bounded, polynomial-time verifiable certificates for both membership and nonmembership, but no uniform deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm?
definitions: For a binary string \(x\), write \(n=|x|\). Membership in \(\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}\) means that there are one polynomial \(q\) and two deterministic polynomial-time Boolean verifiers \(V_1,V_0\) such that, for every \(x\), \[x\in L\iff\exists y\in\{0,1\}^{\leq q(n)}:V_1(x,y)=1,\qquad x\notin L\iff\exists z\in\{0,1\}^{\leq q(n)}:V_0(x,z)=1.\] In particular, no input has accepted certificates of both types and every input has an accepted certificate of one type. Verifier time is polynomial in the combined bit length. Use the shared definition of [P](definitions.html#p-np). The proposed language must defeat every such machine and polynomial bound. Algorithms have no advice, oracle or random bits. This is a total language-class comparison, not a promise problem or a requirement to output certificates. Witness lengths and machines are uniform over all input lengths.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of a language in \((\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP})\setminus\mathrm{P}\), including both verifiers and an unconditional uniform lower bound, or prove that every language satisfying the two verifier conditions belongs to \(\mathrm{P}\). An unproved hardness assumption, a promise-problem separation or hardness of finding witnesses alone does not decide this statement.

title: Existence of TFNP-complete problems
summary: TFNP contains search problems with polynomially bounded, efficiently verifiable answers guaranteed to exist for every binary input. The question asks whether one problem in this class is complete for all the others under deterministic polynomial-time many-one search reductions. Each reduction makes one transformed instance and must decode every valid returned answer correctly. The complete relation is fixed universally, while the reduction and its polynomial bounds may vary with the source problem. Known subclass completeness and oracle results clarify the structure without settling this general existence question.
formal:
Does the class of total polynomially bounded search problems with polynomial-time verifiable answers contain a complete problem under deterministic polynomial-time many-one search reductions?

Writing this class as \(\mathrm{TFNP}\) and the reduction as \(\le_m^p\), the target is
\[\exists Q\in\mathrm{TFNP}\ \forall R\in\mathrm{TFNP},\qquad R\le_m^p Q.\]
The same fixed relation \(Q\) must work for every \(R\). For each \(R\), a reduction computes one \(Q\)-instance from the input and converts every valid answer to that instance into a valid \(R\)-answer. The question is unrelativized and concerns the whole class, including problems whose totality follows from different mathematical principles.
definitions:
Use [TFNP](definitions.html#counting) on all finite binary strings, including the empty input. The relation is decidable by a deterministic polynomial-time verifier, every input has an answer, and every valid answer obeys the relation's fixed polynomial length bound.

Use the [many-one search reduction](definitions.html#reductions) \(R\le_m^p Q\) with maps \(F,G\). Encode the pair for \(G\) as \(1^{|x|}0xz\). Both maps are total uniform bit algorithms and may return a fixed output on malformed tuple encodings. The decoder receives the original \(x\) and must work for every \(z\) satisfying \(Q(F(x),z)\).

A complete \(Q\) is chosen before \(R\). The maps and their polynomial bounds can depend on the pair. The negation is \(\forall Q\in\mathrm{TFNP}\ \exists R\in\mathrm{TFNP}: R\not\le_m^p Q\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the existence statement. An affirmative answer must specify one relation \(Q\), prove its polynomial balance, deterministic polynomial-time verifiability and totality on all binary inputs, and establish the stated reductions from every \(R\in\mathrm{TFNP}\). A negative answer must prove that every candidate \(Q\in\mathrm{TFNP}\) fails to receive such a reduction from some relation in the class. No effective enumeration of all TFNP problems is additionally required. A subclass-completeness result, a separation relative to an oracle or a conditional consequence alone is insufficient.

title: NL versus UL
summary: NL permits many accepting computation branches while using only logarithmic workspace. UL requires exactly one accepting branch on a yes input and none on a no input. The computation must have exactly one accepting branch on each reachable input. Hoza constructs a logspace generator of weights isolating minimum paths in layered directed graphs. Applying the Reinhardt–Allender simulation yields the uniform equality NL = UL.
formal:
Is \(\mathrm{NL}=\mathrm{UL}\)? Equivalently, do there exist one nondeterministic Turing machine \(M\) and constants \(C,D,k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) such that, on every explicitly encoded directed-reachability input \(x=(G,s,t)\) of bit length \(N\), every computation branch halts within \(D(N+2)^k\) steps and visits at most \(C\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil\) work-tape cells, and
\[\#\{\text{accepting computation branches of }M(x)\}=
\begin{cases}1,&t\text{ is reachable from }s\text{ in }G,\\0,&\text{otherwise}?\end{cases}\]
The constants and machine are independent of the input. Unreachable and malformed inputs must have no accepting branch.
definitions:
The vertex set is \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge1\). Use a self-delimiting explicit binary list of all vertices and all directed edges, together with \(s,t\in[n]\). In particular, isolated vertices are represented and \(N\ge n\); a binary vertex count is not a succinct description of an exponentially large graph. Edges are ordered pairs of vertices. Self-loops are allowed, and repeated edge entries may be interpreted as the same edge. A directed path from \(s\) to \(t\) follows the listed edge directions, and the length-zero path is allowed when \(s=t\). No planarity, acyclicity, bounded-degree or unique-path promise is present. Invalid list structure or out-of-range vertices make the encoding malformed. Validity is deterministically checkable in logarithmic space, by rescanning the input if needed. Explicit adjacency lists, edge lists and adjacency matrices are interchangeable here through deterministic logarithmic-space reductions of polynomial output length.

The machine has a finite description with a fixed finite nondeterministic transition relation, one two-way read-only input tape bounded by endmarkers, and a fixed number of initially blank read/write work tapes over finite alphabets. Heads use ordinary Turing-machine moves. The space bound counts all distinct work-tape cells visited on a branch, including blank cells crossed, counters and every temporary record. Input cells and finite control do not count. The output is acceptance or rejection. No advice, randomness, oracle, writable input, catalytic tape or other uncharged storage is available. Every branch, including a rejecting branch, obeys the same polynomial clock and logarithmic-space bounds.

A computation branch is a complete sequence of transition choices from the initial configuration to halting. Two sequences that merge into the same configuration still count as distinct branches. The condition counts successful computations, not distinct accepting configurations, output values, graph paths or certificates after identifying equivalent strings. Rejecting branches need not be unique. The machine is not required to output the graph path or to behave deterministically.

For languages of binary strings, \(\mathrm{NL}\) is acceptance by nondeterministic machines under these time and space bounds, allowing any positive number of accepting branches on a yes input and none on a no input. The subclass \(\mathrm{UL}\) requires at most one accepting branch on every input, hence exactly one on a yes input. A polynomial all-branch clock is the usual equivalent convention for logarithmic-space acceptance. The class equality quantifies separately over languages and machines: every language in NL must have some UL machine. It does not additionally require an effective compiler mapping descriptions of arbitrary NL machines to UL machines.

Directed reachability is NL-complete under deterministic logarithmic-space many-one reductions. Such reductions preserve the answer and can be composed with a UL machine by deterministically recomputing required output bits; this does not add accepting branches. Its membership in UL therefore implies \(\mathrm{NL}\subseteq\mathrm{UL}\); the reverse inclusion follows from the definitions.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of \(\mathrm{NL}=\mathrm{UL}\) for the specified uniform model. An affirmative reachability construction must supply one machine and fixed constants and establish its exact accepting-branch count, correctness on all inputs, and every-branch time and space bounds. A negative answer must prove that some NL language is outside UL, equivalently exclude every proposed reachability machine with these guarantees; the class/reachability equivalence must be justified if used. The graph itself may have arbitrarily many paths, so a promise of a unique graph path cannot replace the required algorithmic unambiguity. A larger-space simulation, nonuniform advice, catalytic memory, an oracle, an unproved hardness assumption or a lower bound only for a restricted isolation procedure does not settle the exact question. No approximate branch count or resource estimate is accepted.

title: Sliding-scale PCP conjecture
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
summary: A PCP verifier checks a fixed proof by inspecting a few selected symbols. The target asks for constant symbol queries, logarithmic randomness, and polynomial proof length and alphabet size. Satisfiable formulas must have a proof accepted on every random string. For an unsatisfiable formula, every proof must be accepted with probability at most a fixed inverse power of the input length. A complete Lean-checked resolution must achieve or rule out all of these guarantees simultaneously for one uniform verifier.
formal:
Do there exist positive integers \(a,b,d,q\), real constants \(c>0\) and \(K>0\), and one uniform deterministic oracle Turing machine \(V\) satisfying the following conditions? For every encoded 3-CNF formula \(F\) of bit length \(N\), set
\[
 r_N=\left\lceil a\log_2(N+2)\right\rceil,\qquad
 M_N=(N+2)^b,\qquad \Sigma_N=\{0,1,\ldots,M_N-1\}.
\]
Given \(F\), a uniformly random string \(R\in\{0,1\}^{r_N}\), and oracle access to a fixed proof \(\pi\in\Sigma_N^{M_N}\), the verifier makes at most \(q\) symbol queries, halts in at most \(K(N+2)^d\) bit operations, and accepts or rejects. It must have perfect completeness and inverse-polynomial soundness:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F\text{ satisfiable}&\ \Longrightarrow\ 
   \exists\pi\ \forall R:\ V^\pi(F,R)=1,\\
 F\text{ unsatisfiable}&\ \Longrightarrow\ 
   \forall\pi:\ \Pr_R[V^\pi(F,R)=1]\le (N+2)^{-c}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All constants and the verifier are independent of \(F\) and \(N\).
definitions:
A Boolean literal is a variable or its negation. A 3-CNF formula is a finite conjunction of clauses, each a disjunction of at most three literals. Satisfiability means that some assignment of Boolean values to all variables appearing in the formula makes every clause true. The empty conjunction is true and an empty clause is false; repeated literals and repeated clauses are allowed.

Fix the following explicit encoding. For a nonnegative integer \(z\), let \(\operatorname{bin}(z)\) be its binary expansion, with \(\operatorname{bin}(0)=0\), and encode it by \(1^t0\operatorname{bin}(z)\), where \(t\) is the expansion length. Encode a formula by its clause count, then for each clause its length in \(\{0,1,2,3\}\), then its literals. A literal is one sign bit followed by the code of its positive integer variable index. There is no additional declared variable count and no trailing data. The parameter \(N\) is the length of this entire binary representation, including indices and delimiters. Invalid encodings may simply be rejected and are not part of the completeness and soundness requirements.

The proof has \(M_N\) addressable locations, each containing one symbol from \(\Sigma_N\).
