Recent strong lower bounds for restricted proofs and the known unrestricted quadratic bound do not settle this question. A resolution would locate a central limitation, or unexpected strength, of propositional reasoning with parity.
formal:
Is resolution over parities not polynomially bounded on unsatisfiable Boolean CNF formulas? Precisely, is the following proposition true?
\[
\forall C,k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \exists F\quad
\bigl[F\text{ is an unsatisfiable CNF}\ \land\
L_{\oplus}(F)>C\bigl(N(F)+1\bigr)^k\bigr].
\]
Here \(L_{\oplus}(F)\) is the minimum number of lines in any unrestricted \(\mathrm{Res}(\oplus)\) refutation of \(F\), with the rules below, and \(N(F)\) is its full combinatorial input size. Earlier proof lines may be reused arbitrarily. There is no restriction on depth, width, regularity or space.
definitions:
The field \(\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}\) has addition and multiplication modulo two. A Boolean assignment to \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is an element of \(\mathbb F_2^n\). A literal is \(x_i\) or \(\neg x_i\); a clause is a finite set of literals interpreted as their disjunction, with the empty clause false. A CNF formula \(F\) is a finite conjunction of clauses. It is unsatisfiable if no assignment makes every clause true. Relabel its distinct occurring variables consecutively as \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\); no unused declared variables are counted. Put
\[
N(F)=n+\#\{\text{clauses of }F\}+
       \sum_{D\text{ a clause of }F}|D|.
\]
The empty conjunction and empty clauses are allowed. Clauses are listed explicitly, with signs and binary variable indices. This input measure is polynomially equivalent to the length of this ordinary explicit binary encoding, so the existence of a polynomial bound does not depend on that encoding choice.

A linear form is \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\), with \(a_i\in\mathbb F_2\), including the zero form. A linear equation is \(f=b\), for \(b\in\mathbb F_2\). A linear clause is a finite disjunction of these equations, again allowing the empty disjunction. Its truth value is given by evaluating all equations over \(\mathbb F_2\). Ordinary positive and negative literals are represented respectively by \(x_i=1\) and \(x_i=0\).

A refutation is a finite sequence of linear clauses ending with the empty clause. Each line is either an input clause of \(F\), translated as above, or follows from earlier lines by one of exactly these rules:

Parity resolution:
\[
\frac{A\vee(f=0)\qquad B\vee(f=1)}{A\vee B},
\]
where \(A,B\) are linear clauses and \(f\) is any linear form in the input variables. Disjunction is taken modulo order and repeated identical disjuncts.

Semantic weakening: from a linear clause \(A\), infer any linear clause \(B\) such that
\[
\forall x\in\mathbb F_2^n,\quad A(x)=1\Longrightarrow B(x)=1.
\]
This rule is implication from one previous line, not arbitrary implication from all input clauses jointly.

All equations use only the variables of \(F\); there are no extension variables, additional axiom schemes or unlisted inference rules. A previous line can serve as a premise arbitrarily many times, giving a directed acyclic proof graph. Size is the total number of lines, including occurrences of input clauses and weakening steps. It is not the sum of the lengths of the equations. Define \(L_{\oplus}(F)\) as the minimum such size. Every unsatisfiable CNF has a refutation since the system contains ordinary resolution.

The constants \(C,k\) are proposed universal bounds; the witnessing formula may depend on both. The question imposes no separate running-time condition on constructing these witnesses and fixes no particular family of formulas. It asks for unconditional non-polynomial boundedness of this fixed proof system, not for a conditional statement assuming a complexity separation.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the displayed proposition or its negation. An affirmative answer must rule out every uniform polynomial line-count upper bound for unrestricted refutations. A negative answer must prove that there are fixed \(C,k\ge1\) such that every unsatisfiable CNF \(F\) has a refutation of at most \(C(N(F)+1)^k\) lines; no efficient proof-finding algorithm is additionally required. Lower bounds confined to tree-like, regular, reversible or bounded-depth proofs do not meet the affirmative target, and a conditional lower bound does not settle the unconditional proposition. No additive numerical tolerance changes this binary asymptotic claim.

title: \(PV_1\) nonprovability of polynomial-time SAT solvers
summary: A polynomial-time SAT search algorithm would return a satisfying assignment whenever one exists. The question asks whether the theory PV1 fails to prove correctness for every such polynomial-time function symbol. This is a statement about finite formal proofs, with the theory and formula encoding specified explicitly. It can hold even if a polynomial-time solver exists but its correctness has no proof in this particular theory. The benchmark requires a complete Lean proof of the nonprovability schema or a verified counterexample consisting of a symbol and a finite correctness proof.
formal: Is it true that, for every unary function symbol \(g\) in the syntactically generated language \(L_{PV}\) below, \[PV_1\not\vdash\Phi_g,\qquad \Phi_g=\forall F\,\forall a\bigl(\operatorname{Sat}(F,a)\to\operatorname{Sat}(F,g(F))\bigr)?\] The theory, admissible symbols and arithmetic formula \(\operatorname{Sat}\) are fixed in the definitions. This is an unconditional assertion about finite first-order proofs.
definitions:
The theory is one-sorted classical first-order arithmetic with equality. We use Jeřábek's explicit presentation of \(PV_1\), cited as an alternative axiomatization by the source survey. Its base language is
\[
L=\{0,S,+,\cdot,\le,\#,\operatorname{len},M\}.
\]
In the intended structure on the nonnegative integers, \(S(x)=x+1\), \(\operatorname{len}(x)=\lceil\log_2(x+1)\rceil\), \(M(x,y)=\lfloor x/2^y\rfloor\), and \(x\#y=2^{\operatorname{len}(x)\operatorname{len}(y)}\). In particular \(\operatorname{len}(0)=0\). Write \(1=S(0)\), \(2=S(S(0))\), \(H(x)=M(x,1)\), and \(x<y\) for \(x\le y\land x\ne y\). These intended interpretations do not supply additional axioms.

The base theory has the universal closures of the following arithmetic axioms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+0&=x,& x+S(y)&=S(x+y),\\
x\cdot0&=0,&x\cdot S(y)&=x\cdot y+x,\\
0&\le x,& S(y)\le x&\ \longleftrightarrow\ y<x,\\
M(x,0)&=x,&
M(x,y)&=2M(x,S(y))\ \lor\ M(x,y)=S(2M(x,S(y))),\\
\operatorname{len}(0)&=0,&
x\ne0&\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{len}(x)=S(\operatorname{len}(H(x))),\\
0\#1&=1,&
x\ne0&\ \longrightarrow\
\bigl(x\#1=2(H(x)\#1)\ \land\
y\#x=(y\#1)(y\#H(x))\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
It also has ordinary induction
\[
[A(0,\vec z)\land\forall x(A(x,\vec z)\to A(S(x),\vec z))]
\to\forall x\,A(x,\vec z)
\]
for every base-language formula \(A\) all of whose quantifiers are sharply bounded. A sharply bounded quantifier is \(\forall v\le\operatorname{len}(t)\) or \(\exists v\le\operatorname{len}(t)\), where \(t\) has no free occurrence of \(v\). A bounded universal quantifier expands to an implication, and a bounded existential quantifier to a conjunction. All induction parameters \(\vec z\) are universally closed.

Generate \(L_{PV}\) syntactically from \(L\) by finitely iterating two rules. For every existing term \(t\) with free variables among \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), add an \(r\)-ary symbol \(f_t\). For every tuple of existing symbols \(g(\vec x),h_0(\vec x,y,z),h_1(\vec x,y,z),b(\vec x,y)\), add a new symbol \(R_{g,h_0,h_1,b}(\vec x,y)\). Arity is finite, the parameter tuple may be empty, and distinct construction trees are distinct symbols even when their intended functions agree. Include the universal closure of \(f_t(\vec x)=t(\vec x)\). For each recursion symbol, abbreviating it by \(R\), include exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
R(\vec x,y)&\le b(\vec x,y),\\
g(\vec x)\le b(\vec x,0)&\to R(\vec x,0)=g(\vec x),\\
y\ne0\land h_0(\vec x,y,R(\vec x,y))\le b(\vec x,2y)
&\to R(\vec x,2y)=h_0(\vec x,y,R(\vec x,y)),\\
h_1(\vec x,y,R(\vec x,y))\le b(\vec x,S(2y))
&\to R(\vec x,S(2y))=h_1(\vec x,y,R(\vec x,y)).
\end{aligned}
\]
These are bounded-recursion constraints; no unconditional recursion equation is added when its bounding test fails.

Finally include polynomial induction
\[
[A(0,\vec z)\land\forall x(A(H(x),\vec z)\to A(x,\vec z))]
\to\forall x\,A(x,\vec z)
\]
for every quantifier-free \(L_{PV}\)-formula \(A\). Together with the base theory and the symbol axioms, these schemes define \(PV_1\) here. A proof is a finite derivation in classical first-order logic with equality from finitely many instances of these schemes. No true-universal arithmetic sentences, consistency assumptions, or external correctness axioms are added. The outer quantifier over unary symbols \(g\) ranges over their finite syntactic construction trees, not over an oracle for deciding which arbitrary programs run in polynomial time.

The SAT relation is fixed arithmetically, rather than by selecting an unspecified polynomial-time evaluator symbol. All abbreviations in this paragraph and below expand into formulas of the base language \(L\). Set \(\ell=\operatorname{len}(F)\), and define
\[
\operatorname{Bit}(x,i)\ \longleftrightarrow\
M(x,i)=2M(x,S(i))+1.
\]
Every auxiliary quantifier over a node, field, index or width is bounded by \(\ell\), with any smaller displayed bound imposed as a guard. Thus these quantifiers are sharply bounded. The one truth-table witness below has a separate bound.

The natural number \(F\) encodes an ordinary propositional formula tree whose nodes are numbered \(0,\ldots,m-1\), with children before their parents. Its variables are \(x_0,\ldots,x_{m-1}\), with unused variables allowed. To define \(\operatorname{Form}(F,w,d,m)\), require \(w,d,m\le\ell\), \(w\ge2\), \(m\ge1\), \(w+d=\ell\), and
\[
\ell=w+2+(1+3m)w.
\]
The least significant \(w\) bits of \(F\) are all one and bit \(w\) is zero. Starting at bit \(w+1\) are \(1+3m\) fields of \(w\) bits, followed by the high sentinel bit one; the exact bit-length equality enforces that sentinel and forbids further bits. Put \(P=M(1\#F,d)\), whose intended value is \(2^w\). Field \(j\) has value \(r\) exactly when
\[
D(F,w,d,j,r)\ \longleftrightarrow\
r<P\ \land\
M(F,w+1+jw)=P\,M(F,w+1+(j+1)w)+r.
\]
Require field zero to have value \(m\). For each node \(i<m\), its fields \(1+3i,2+3i,3+3i\) have values \(\tau_i,u_i,v_i\), respectively. This notation abbreviates existentially quantified numbers at most \(\ell\) satisfying their three \(D\) relations, not new function symbols. Every record must satisfy exactly the relevant one of these four cases:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\tau_i & \text{record restrictions} & \text{meaning}\\
0 & u_i<m,\ v_i=0 & x_{u_i}\\
1 & u_i<i,\ v_i=0 & \neg\text{ child }u_i\\
2 & u_i<i,\ v_i<i & \text{child }u_i\land\text{child }v_i\\
3 & u_i<i,\ v_i<i & \text{child }u_i\lor\text{child }v_i .
\end{array}
\]
Every node \(i\) with \(S(i)<m\) must occur in exactly one child slot of all records, and the node \(r\) with \(S(r)=m\) in no child slot. Specifically, slot \((j,0)\) contains \(i\) when \(j<m,\tau_j\in\{1,2,3\},u_j=i\); slot \((j,1)\) contains \(i\) when \(j<m,\tau_j\in\{2,3\},v_j=i\). Denote this relation by \(C(j,s,i)\), with other slot values false. Exactly one means
\[
\exists j,s\le\ell\
[C(j,s,i)\land
\forall k,t\le\ell\,(C(k,t,i)\to(k=j\land t=s))].
\]
Together the record restrictions, field conditions and child-slot conditions define \(\operatorname{Form}\). In particular this encodes a tree, with no shared subtrees or circuit gates.

Define \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,a,v,w,d,m)\) by requiring, at every node \(i<m\), the following biconditional for the indicated record type:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\tau_i & \operatorname{Bit}(v,i)\text{ is equivalent to}\\
0 & \operatorname{Bit}(a,u_i)\\
1 & \neg\operatorname{Bit}(v,u_i)\\
2 & \operatorname{Bit}(v,u_i)\land\operatorname{Bit}(v,v_i)\\
3 & \operatorname{Bit}(v,u_i)\lor\operatorname{Bit}(v,v_i).
\end{array}
\]
Here \(v\) is the numeric table witness and \(v_i\) the second child field; their names designate different bound variables when the abbreviations are expanded. Now set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Sat}(F,a)\ \longleftrightarrow\
\exists w,d,m,e\le\ell\ \exists v<1\#F\
[&\operatorname{Form}(F,w,d,m)\land e+m=\ell\\
 &\land a<M(1\#F,e)
 \land\operatorname{Eval}(F,a,v,w,d,m)\\
 &\land\exists r\le\ell\,(S(r)=m\land\operatorname{Bit}(v,r))].
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(a\) is an assignment of \(m\) bits, allowing leading zeroes, and the first \(m\) bits of \(v\) are the values of the formula nodes with true root. The bound \(1\#F\) is \(2^\ell\), so the table has only linearly many bits in the input bit length. Malformed formula codes make \(\operatorname{Sat}\) false. No unrestricted exponentiation symbol or semantic SAT predicate is added to the theory.

For each syntactically generated unary symbol \(g\), let
\[
\Phi_g=\forall F\,\forall a\,
(\operatorname{Sat}(F,a)\to\operatorname{Sat}(F,g(F))).
\]
It asserts search correctness on every satisfiable formula. It imposes no required output on an unsatisfiable formula. The claim concerns absence of finite \(PV_1\) proofs of these sentences, not absence of semantically correct polynomial-time solvers as a separate assumption.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof that no generated unary symbol has a finite first-order derivation of its displayed SAT-search correctness sentence from the stated PV1 axioms, or a complete Lean proof of the negation, exhibiting a particular symbol and a valid finite derivation. The formalization must implement the stated syntactic theory and arithmetic SAT relation; any substitute SAT encoding or axiomatization must be proved to preserve the relevant provability claim. Neither assuming P differs from NP, adding all true universal arithmetic axioms, checking finitely many proofs, nor proving only a conditional statement settles this target.

title: Lovász–Schrijver simulation of Cutting Planes
summary: The question asks whether every Cutting Planes refutation has a polynomially longer Lovász–Schrijver refutation. Both systems start from the same real linear inequalities over Boolean variables. Length counts proof lines, with real coefficients unrestricted and earlier lines freely reusable. The reverse simulation is known to fail, and the failure of tree-like LS simulation does not settle the general DAG case. The formulation uses an existence theorem for short proofs, without requiring an efficient proof-conversion algorithm.
formal:
Does the basic Lovász–Schrijver system \(\mathrm{LS}\) polynomially simulate Cutting Planes \(\mathrm{CP}\) in the following real-coefficient, line-count sense?

There exist a real constant \(C\ge1\) and an integer \(k\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), every \(m\ge0\), every finite initial system
\[
\Phi=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}x_j\ge b_i:1\le i\le m\right\},
\qquad a_{ij},b_i\in\mathbb R,
\]
and every CP refutation \(\Pi\) of \(\Phi\), there is an LS refutation \(\Lambda\) of the same initial system satisfying
\[
|\Lambda|\le C\bigl(n+m+|\Pi|+1\bigr)^k.
\]
All variables are Boolean. The proof systems and the length measure are defined below. The constants are independent of the initial coefficients and both proofs.
definitions:
A line is an inequality \(f(x)\ge0\). Polynomials are over \(\mathbb R\) in the original variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\); algebraically identical polynomials are identified by collecting coefficients. The initial lines are the members of \(\Phi\), written with the right-hand side moved to the left. Boolean axioms \(x_j\ge0\) and \(1-x_j\ge0\) are available. The harmless constant axioms \(0\ge0\) and \(1\ge0\) are also permitted; they can be derived from the Boolean axioms with constantly many steps.

Both systems permit nonnegative linear combination: from earlier lines \(f\ge0\) and \(g\ge0\), derive \(\alpha f+\beta g\ge0\) for any \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). Coefficients are exact real numbers. Combining any finite number of earlier lines instead of two changes length by at most a polynomial factor, so the binary version fixes a definite convention.

CP contains only affine-linear lines. Its additional rounding rule is
\[
\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{n}c_jx_j\ge d}
{\sum_{j=1}^{n}c_jx_j\ge\lceil d\rceil},
\qquad c_1,\ldots,c_n\in\mathbb Z,\ d\in\mathbb R.
\]
The rounding premise must have integer variable coefficients; the right side and intermediate combination coefficients may be real. Rounding is justified by the Boolean, hence integer, values of the variables.

Basic LS contains lines of degree at most two. In addition to the common rules and axioms it permits both \(x_j^2-x_j\ge0\) and \(x_j-x_j^2\ge0\). From an earlier affine-linear inequality \(f\ge0\), it may derive \(x_jf\ge0\), or \((1-x_j)f\ge0\), as one line each. Multiplication is permitted only for an affine-linear premise. Nonnegative combination may combine linear or quadratic lines. The source’s linear weakening rule \(a\cdot x\ge d\Rightarrow a\cdot x\ge d'\) for \(d'\le d\) is permitted; it is also obtainable by adding a nonnegative multiple of \(1\ge0\). There is no unrestricted multiplication rule, no rule freely adding arbitrary squares, and no rounding rule in LS. Boolean reduction of quadratic monomials must be justified by the displayed axioms; equality merely on Boolean assignments is not free algebraic rewriting.

A refutation is a finite sequence of justified lines ending with \(-1\ge0\), equivalently \(0\ge1\). Any negative constant conclusion can be normalized by a positive scalar in one further step. An earlier line may be used any number of times: proofs are directed acyclic graphs, not necessarily trees. There are no auxiliary extension variables. Length \(|\Pi|\) is the number of listed lines, counting each occurrence of an initial inequality or axiom that appears, and each derived line. Reuse adds no copy unless a new line is written.

No bound is imposed on the magnitude or bit representation of real coefficients, and no effective transformation from \(\Pi\) to \(\Lambda\) is requested. The statement quantifies mathematically over finite systems of real inequalities; its size parameters count variables, initial inequalities and proof lines. This is the convention, not a bit-size or polynomial-time simulation assertion.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the uniform polynomial line-count assertion. A positive answer must prove the existence of the LS refutation bound for every allowed CP refutation and initial system. A negative answer must show that every candidate polynomial bound fails for some allowed initial system and CP proof. A lower bound restricted to tree-like LS, a simulation only with restricted coefficients, or the already known separation in the opposite direction does not decide this statement. No numerical \(1/100\) tolerance applies to this binary assertion.

title: Polynomial resolution length from logarithmic clause space
summary: A resolution refutation certifies that no assignment satisfies a Boolean formula. Clause space counts how many clauses must be retained at once, and length counts how many clauses are downloaded or inferred. The question asks whether logarithmic minimum clause space always guarantees polynomial minimum length for formulas with bounded input-clause width. The short proof may use more memory than the small-space proof, so simultaneous time–space tradeoffs are a different question. Known results give polynomial length for constant space and quasipolynomial length for logarithmic space, leaving the requested improvement unresolved in the checked literature.
formal:
Does logarithmic clause space imply polynomial refutation length for every fixed input clause width in general resolution?

Precisely, for every fixed integer \(k\ge1\) and real constant \(a>0\), do there exist constants \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), depending only on \(k,a\), such that every unsatisfiable \(k\)-CNF formula \(F\) satisfies
\[\operatorname{Sp}(F)\le a\log_2 N(F)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad L(F)\le B\,N(F)^d?\]
Here \(N(F)=2+|F|+\sum_{C\in F}|C|\) is formula size, \(\operatorname{Sp}(F)\) is the minimum number of clauses simultaneously retained in a resolution refutation, and \(L(F)\) is its minimum number of axiom downloads and inference steps. These two minima are taken independently over all general resolution refutations. The short refutation whose existence is requested has no space restriction.
definitions:
A Boolean variable takes values in \(\{0,1\}\). A literal is a variable or its negation, and a clause is a finite set of literals interpreted as their disjunction. Clauses contain no repeated literal and no complementary pair \(x,\neg x\). The empty clause \(\bot\) is false. A CNF formula is a finite set of clauses interpreted as their conjunction; it is unsatisfiable if no assignment to its variables makes every clause true. A \(k\)-CNF has at most \(k\) literals in every input clause. The fixed input-width parameter \(k\) does not bound clauses derived during a proof.

The variable universe for a proof is the finite set of variables occurring in \(F\). Renaming these variables has no cost. The size \(N(F)\) counts input clauses and literal occurrences, with the added constant two ensuring that its logarithm is positive. Input clauses are a set, so padding by duplicate clauses does not change the formula or its size. If a concrete binary encoding is needed, number the occurring variables consecutively, encode each literal by its index and sign, and list clauses with delimiters. For fixed \(k\), this encoding and the stated combinatorial size are polynomially related; the logarithmic-space versus polynomial-length question is invariant under this choice of size convention.

A resolution refutation is a finite sequence of configurations \(\mathcal D_0,\ldots,\mathcal D_T\), each a set of clauses over the input variables. Initially \(\mathcal D_0=\varnothing\), and the final configuration contains \(\bot\). Each step performs exactly one of the following operations. It may download one input clause \(C\in F\) into memory, adding it to the current set. It may erase one currently retained clause. It may add a resolvent \(C\cup D\) from two currently retained premises \(C\cup\{x\}\) and \(D\cup\{\neg x\}\), where neither \(C\) nor \(D\) contains the pivot variable and the resolvent is non-tautological. It may also weaken a retained clause by adding literals, provided the result is a clause over the same variables. These are the ordinary syntactic resolution and weakening rules. Arbitrary semantic consequence is not an additional inference rule.

Premises must be present before an inference, and they remain present after it unless erased in subsequent steps. An inference adds its conclusion before any such erasure, so the temporary memory needed to hold the conclusion is counted. An erased clause must be downloaded or derived again before reuse. The input formula itself is available for downloads without occupying working memory. Resolution proofs may share intermediate results arbitrarily; neither the tree-like restriction nor the regularity restriction forbidding repeated pivots on a proof path is imposed. No extension variables, stronger proof rules, randomization or error are allowed.

For a refutation \(\pi\), define
\[\operatorname{Sp}(\pi)=\max_{0\le t\le T}|\mathcal D_t|,\]
and let \(L(\pi)\) be its number of axiom-download and inference steps, with repetitions counted. Erasures are not counted in length. One can instead count all steps without changing polynomial-length bounds, because useful erasures can be bounded by the number of additions. Clause space counts each stored clause as one object regardless of its width. It is different from total literal space \(\max_t\sum_{C\in\mathcal D_t}|C|\), from the number of distinct variables in memory, and from the number of stored bits.

For an unsatisfiable formula, resolution completeness guarantees that the following finite integer minima exist:
\[\operatorname{Sp}(F)=\min_{\pi:F\vdash\bot}\operatorname{Sp}(\pi),\qquad L(F)=\min_{\pi:F\vdash\bot}L(\pi).\]
The refutation attaining the first minimum may have very large length. The question is whether a possibly different refutation of polynomial length must nevertheless exist whenever that minimum space is logarithmic.

The full quantifier order is \(\forall k\ge1\;\forall a>0\;\exists B>0,d\ge1\;\forall F\). The exponent \(d\) may depend on the input-width bound and the constant multiplying the logarithm, but not on the individual formula or its size. The proposition does not demand one exponent uniform in all \(k,a\), a procedure finding the short proof, or a transformation that keeps the original space bound.

A negative answer means that for some fixed \(k\) and \(a>0\), no polynomial bounds the minimum length throughout this class: for every \(B>0\) and \(d\ge1\), some unsatisfiable \(k\)-CNF \(F\) has \(\operatorname{Sp}(F)\le a\log_2 N(F)\) but \(L(F)>B N(F)^d\). Thus it must establish genuinely superpolynomial unrestricted resolution length despite the small-space refutation. Merely proving that all proofs which retain small space are long does not refute the proposition.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the quantified implication. A positive answer must establish a polynomial length bound for all promised formulas, with its dependence on fixed \(k,a\) explicit or provably existent. A negative answer must prove the stated logical negation against all polynomial length bounds, including unrestricted-space refutations. A quasipolynomial upper bound, a theorem for constant clause space only, a result for tree-like resolution only, or a simultaneous length–space tradeoff does not settle the target. The statement is an exact asymptotic proposition; additive numerical tolerance is inapplicable.

title: Log-rank conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: Alice and Bob must exactly evaluate a total Boolean function while each receives only one part of its input. The conjecture asks whether their minimum worst-case deterministic communication is bounded by one universal polynomial in logarithmic real matrix rank. The protocol may use arbitrary interaction and local computation, but all input pairs must be handled correctly. A refutation must defeat every universal polynomial, rather than a single proposed constant or exponent. Google’s Cogentic manuscript improves the rank exponent in the upper bound to 0.499995, leaving a polylogarithmic bound in rank open.
formal: Do there exist integers \(C\ge1,k\ge1\) such that every total Boolean function \(f:X\times Y\to\{0,1\}\), for arbitrary nonempty finite sets X and Y, satisfies \(D(f)\le C\bigl(\log_2(r(f)+2)\bigr)^k\)? Here r(f) is the rank over the real numbers of its zero-one communication matrix, and D(f) is its exact deterministic communication complexity in bits.
definitions: Alice receives \(x\in X\), Bob receives \(y\in Y\), and both know the complete function f, its finite domains and their chosen protocol. These shared data are not charged as communication. A protocol is a finite rooted binary tree. Each internal node specifies its sender and a function from that sender’s input set to \(\{0,1\}\). At that node the sender transmits this one bit, and both parties follow the corresponding edge; the node already records the preceding transcript. Every leaf is labeled 0 or 1. For every pair (x,y), the reached leaf must be labeled f(x,y), so both parties determine the exact answer. The cost is the maximum number of transmitted bits on any input pair, equivalently the tree depth after deleting unreachable branches. D(f) is the minimum cost among all correct trees; a finite protocol always exists. The protocol may depend arbitrarily on f, and its description length, local computation and number of communication rounds have no separate bound or charge. The communication matrix is \(M_f=(f(x,y))_{x\in X,y\in Y}\), treating its zeroes and ones as real scalars. Define \(r(f)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}(M_f)\), the dimension of its column span over \(\mathbb R\). The particular enumeration of either domain does not matter. Rank zero means the all-zero function, which has D(f)=0, and the all-one function also has D(f)=0. The term r+2 avoids a zero or undefined logarithm at small ranks without changing the asymptotic conjecture. The same C and k must work for every choice of domains and function; the protocol need not be generated uniformly from the table. The statement has no promise pairs, missing matrix entries, distribution on inputs, randomness, quantum messages, approximation or one-way restriction. Rank over a finite field, approximate rank and sign rank are not the parameter used here. Some sources encode outputs by minus one and plus one. With \(A=2M_f-J\), where J is the all-one matrix, the two ordinary real ranks differ by at most one and the output relabeling does not change D(f); with the r+2 convention these formulations have the same polynomial-boundedness question. The explicit negation is: for every pair of integers C,k at least one, there exist nonempty finite X,Y and a total f such that \(D(f)>C(\log_2(r(f)+2))^k\). No effective generator of the counterexample functions is added.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of a single pair of universal constants C,k satisfying the displayed inequality, or prove its quantified negation excluding every such pair. An affirmative proof must apply to every total function in the exact interactive protocol model; it need not compute an optimal protocol efficiently. A negative proof must give arbitrarily strong failures of polynomial dependence on log-rank, with examples permitted to depend on C and k. Failure of one proposed exponent, a result for partial functions, or a bound using approximate rank, sign rank, randomness or quantum communication does not meet this target.

title: Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: A scalar Boolean function has a Fourier spectrum whose squared coefficients form a probability distribution on sets of input coordinates. The Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture asks whether its Shannon entropy is at most a universal constant times the expected size of a spectral set. Every dimension and every Boolean function are included, with uniform inputs, base-two entropy and exactly normalized bit-flip influence. A complete Lean-checked answer must prove the universal bound or show that the ratio is unbounded over nonconstant Boolean functions. The conjecture would imply fixed-accuracy Fourier concentration for DNF formulas, while weaker coordinate-entropy estimates and quantum counterexamples leave its classical target unsettled.
formal: Does there exist one finite real constant \(C>0\) such that, for every positive integer \(n\) and every function \(f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\}\), \[H(f)\le C I(f),\] where \(H(f)\) is the Shannon entropy in bits of the squared Fourier spectrum and \(I(f)\) is total influence for uniformly distributed inputs? The same \(C\) must work for all dimensions and all Boolean functions.
definitions: Let \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and give each \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) probability \(2^{-n}\). For \(S\subseteq[n]\), define \(\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i\), with empty product one, and \[\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x),\qquad q_S=\widehat f(S)^2.\] These are real coefficients and \(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}q_S=1\). Define \(\eta(0)=0\) and \(\eta(t)=t\log_2(1/t)\) for \(0<t\le1\), where \(\log_2 t=\ln t/\ln2\). Then \[H(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\eta(q_S).\] The sum includes the empty set and is not conditioned on nonempty spectral subsets or divided by the variance. For each \(i\in[n]\), let \(x^{\oplus i}\) negate coordinate \(i\) and retain all other coordinates. Set \[I_i(f)=2^{-n}\bigl|\{x\in\{-1,1\}^n:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\}\bigr|,\qquad I(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n I_i(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|q_S.\] Influence uses an actual bit flip, with no additional probability of leaving that coordinate unchanged. All scalar Boolean functions are allowed; no balance, monotonicity, circuit-size, degree or efficient-computability promise is imposed. Constant functions satisfy \(H(f)=I(f)=0\). The inequality is non-strict, so it includes them.
answer_criterion: Provide a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal inequality for some positive finite constant, or of its logical negation. A positive proof must use the specified uniform measure, full squared spectrum, base-two Shannon entropy and total bit-flip influence for every \(n\) and every scalar Boolean function. A negative proof must establish \[\forall C>0\ \exists n\ge1\ \exists f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\},\quad H(f)>C I(f).\] The dimension and function may depend on \(C\); equivalently, the entropy-to-influence ratios of nonconstant Boolean functions must be unbounded. Defeating one numerical constant or checking finitely many truth tables is insufficient. No optimal value of \(C\), algorithm for finding counterexamples or numerical approximation is required.
references: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~jswright/papers/fei.pdf | https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08271 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00246 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01424 | https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.2651 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03117 | https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04411

title: Mansour’s conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: A short DNF describes a Boolean function using a small number of conjunctions. Mansour’s conjecture asks whether such a function can always be approximated by retaining only a small number of its ordinary Fourier coefficients. The permitted discarded squared mass is epsilon under uniformly random Boolean inputs. The retained number must be at most the term count raised to a universal constant times log of inverse epsilon, with no dependence on the ambient dimension. A complete Lean-checked answer must prove or refute this strong bound for all DNFs and all stated accuracies, without an algorithmic recovery requirement.
formal:
Does there exist an absolute real constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), integer \(s\ge2\), function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\) representable by a DNF with at most \(s\) terms, and real \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\), there is a family \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}\) for which
\[
 |\mathcal F|\le\left\lceil s^{C\log_2(1/\varepsilon)}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 \sum_{S\subseteq[n],\ S\notin\mathcal F}\widehat f(S)^2\le\varepsilon?
\]
The coefficients are the ordinary Walsh–Fourier coefficients under the uniform distribution. The same constant \(C\) must work for every dimension, term count, formula and accuracy.
definitions:
Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and let \(2^{[n]}\) be its set of subsets. A literal is either the condition \(x_i=1\) or the condition \(x_i=-1\). A term is a conjunction of literals; a disjunctive normal form (DNF) is an OR of terms. Its represented function has value \(+1\) when at least one term is satisfied and \(-1\) otherwise. The number of terms, rather than the total number of literal occurrences, is the size parameter \(s\). Each term may contain any number of variables; variables may occur in arbitrarily many terms, and terms may overlap. Empty conjunctions and an empty disjunction have their usual constant meanings. The statement asks only for existence of some representation with at most \(s\) terms.

For every \(S\subseteq[n]\), define the parity character and its coefficient by
\[
 \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i,\qquad \chi_{\varnothing}(x)=1,
 \qquad
 \widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x).
\]
These characters form an orthonormal basis for real functions on the uniform Boolean cube, with inner product \(\mathbb E[g(X)h(X)]\) for uniform \(X\). In particular,
\[
 f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x),
 \qquad \sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2=1.
\]
The empty-set coefficient is included in these sums and may belong to \(\mathcal F\).

Keeping the coefficients indexed by \(\mathcal F\) gives the real multilinear polynomial
\[
 g_{\mathcal F}(x)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal F}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x),
\]
whose mean squared error is exactly
\[
 \mathbb E[(f(X)-g_{\mathcal F}(X))^2]
   =\sum_{S\notin\mathcal F}\widehat f(S)^2.
\]
Thus \(\varepsilon\) measures discarded squared Fourier mass, without an additional normalization factor. The approximant need not be Boolean-valued. The bound concerns the number of retained characters, not their maximum degree, pointwise error or disagreement probability.

The family \(\mathcal F\) may depend on the function and on \(\varepsilon\). No efficient algorithm for discovering it, producing the coefficients or learning the function is required. There is no promise on a DNF’s read number, which is the maximum number of its terms containing any one variable, and no random distribution on formulas. The only input distribution in the approximation is uniform on \(\{-1,1\}^n\).

This is the strong accuracy-dependent form of the conjecture. Allowing \(s^{K(\varepsilon)}\) characters for an arbitrary function \(K\) of the error would be a weaker target. Here that exponent must be bounded by one constant times \(\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\), uniformly even when \(\varepsilon\) decreases with \(n\) or \(s\).
answer_criterion:
Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the displayed statement with one universal \(C\), or a complete Lean-checked proof of its negation.

A negative answer must show that for every \(C>0\) there are admissible \(n,s,\varepsilon,f\) for which every family of at most \(\lceil s^{C\log_2(1/\varepsilon)}\rceil\) characters leaves discarded squared mass greater than \(\varepsilon\). Defeating only one proposed constant does not refute existence of another. A theorem only for random DNFs, bounded-read formulas, fixed width or a different input distribution does not cover the target. A polynomial concentration bound with unspecified dependence of its exponent on \(\varepsilon\) establishes only the weaker form. This is an exact universal proposition; the benchmark’s numerical \(1/100\) tolerance is not a replacement for its full range of error parameters.

title: Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: The Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture concerns real multilinear polynomials whose values lie between zero and one on every point of the Boolean cube. It asks for a variable whose mean squared influence is bounded below by a fixed power of variance divided by degree, independent of the number of variables. The universal claim includes arbitrary real coefficients and arbitrarily small positive variance, with one normalization and one exponent throughout. A complete Lean proof must establish that claim or provide violations for every proposed exponent, rather than only a particular numerical power. The conjecture would imply almost-everywhere classical query simulation, while known random-restriction, bounded-round and completely bounded results leave its full scalar form unresolved.
formal:
Does there exist a positive integer \(C\) such that for every integer \(n\ge1\), every integer \(1\le d\le n\), and every real multilinear polynomial \(f\) in \(n\) variables of degree at most \(d\),
\[\bigl[\forall x\in\{-1,1\}^n,\ 0\le f(x)\le1\bigr]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\exists i\in[n]:\ \operatorname{Inf}_i(f)\ge\left(\frac{\operatorname{Var}(f)}d\right)^C?\]
Variance and squared \(L_2\) influence use the uniform distribution on the entire Boolean cube, with the normalization below. The same exponent \(C\) must work for all dimensions, degrees, coefficients and variances.
definitions:
Polynomials and domain. Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\chi_S(x)=\prod_{j\in S}x_j\) for \(S\subseteq[n]\), with \(\chi_{\varnothing}=1\). A real multilinear polynomial is a finite sum
\[f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x),\qquad a_S\in\mathbb R.\]
Multilinear means that each variable has exponent at most one in each monomial. Degree at most \(d\) means \(a_S=0\) whenever \(|S|>d\). The range restriction \(0\le f(x)\le1\) is required at every one of the \(2^n\) sign vectors. No range condition away from this cube is imposed.

Uniform averages and Fourier coefficients. For any real-valued function \(h\) on the cube, define \(\mathbb E h=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}h(x)\). The characters \(\chi_S\) give the unique multilinear representation on the cube, with
\[\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E[f(x)\chi_S(x)]=a_S.\]
In particular \(\widehat f(\varnothing)=\mathbb Ef\). Variance is
\[\operatorname{Var}(f)=\mathbb E[(f-\mathbb Ef)^2]=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2.\]
For the stated range, \(0\le\operatorname{Var}(f)\le1/4\).

Influence. Let \(x^{\oplus i}\) be obtained from \(x\) by negating its \(i\)-th coordinate and leaving all others fixed. Set
\[D_if(x)=\frac{f(x)-f(x^{\oplus i})}{2},\qquad \operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=\mathbb E[(D_if)^2]=\frac14\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^{\oplus i}))^2]=\sum_{S\ni i}\widehat f(S)^2.\]
This is a mean squared difference, not the probability that the two function values differ, their mean absolute difference, or the maximum change over inputs. All sums and expectations in the target use this same uniform measure.

Scope and quantifiers. Coefficients are arbitrary real numbers, without a rationality, description-length or computability restriction. The statement is an existence inequality, not a demand for an algorithm finding the coordinate. The coordinate may depend on the whole polynomial. No sparsity, block decomposition, common coefficient magnitude, Boolean-output, nonnegativity-of-coefficients or realizability-by-quantum-algorithms promise is present. There is no positive lower threshold on variance. Constant polynomials have zero variance and all influences zero, so every coordinate satisfies the inequality for them. The degree parameter is a positive upper bound, so division by zero never occurs.

Normalization of the exponent. Allowing any real \(C\ge1\) gives an equivalent assertion: for \(0\le v/d\le1/4\), increasing the exponent to a positive integer only decreases the right-hand side. A bound of the usual form \(c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^a/d^b\), with fixed positive constants \(c,a,b\), also yields this formulation after increasing \(C\). Thus the one-exponent statement records polynomial dependence without selecting a particular best exponent or a hidden constant depending on \(n\).
answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal existence claim or its negation. A positive answer must prove one exponent works simultaneously for every allowed \(n,d,f\), including arbitrarily small positive variance. No optimal exponent or algorithm for computing an influential coordinate is required.

A negative answer must prove that for every positive integer \(C\) there exist integers \(n\ge1\), \(1\le d\le n\), and an admissible polynomial of positive variance such that
\[\forall i\in[n],\quad\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)<\left(\frac{\operatorname{Var}(f)}d\right)^C.\]
The dimension, degree and polynomial may depend on \(C\). A rigorously specified family with those properties qualifies; a counterexample to just one proposed exponent does not negate the existence of another universal exponent. Numerical estimates must be certified strongly enough to establish the exact pointwise range and strict influence inequalities they assert.

A theorem only for Boolean-valued outputs, completely bounded forms, boundedly many quantum-query rounds, or a positive fraction of randomly restricted functions does not by itself cover the full polynomial class. An exponential dependence on degree is also weaker than the requested polynomial bound. This is a yes-or-no conjecture with an exact inequality, not a numerical target subject to additive 1/100 tolerance.

title: Interactive compression with logarithmic input-length overhead
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: The underlying question concerns two-party interactive communication, even though its source article studies multiparty protocols. A protocol can transmit many more bits than its internal information cost under the input distribution. The proposed precise target allows a logarithmic factor in input bit length and a fixed total-variation error when both parties reconstruct the transcript. Exact compression without loss is already known to fail, while results for external information or independent inputs address different targets. A complete Lean answer must prove this explicitly specified universal simulation bound or a lower bound refuting every proposed universal constant.
formal:
Is there an absolute constant \(K\in\mathbb R,\ K\ge1\) such that every two-party protocol \(\pi\) on \(n\)-bit inputs, under every joint input distribution \(\mu\), has a simulation \(\rho\) with distributional error at most \(1/100\) and worst-case communication at most
\[
K\bigl(I_{\mu}(\pi)+1\bigr)\bigl\lceil\log_2(n+2)\bigr\rceil\quad\text{bits}?
\]
Here \(n\ge1\), the protocol and simulation model, internal information cost \(I_{\mu}\), and joint-transcript error are defined below. There is no restriction on the finite communication cost of \(\pi\), and \(K\) must be independent of \(n,\mu,\pi\).

This is an explicitly selected editorial version of the source's proposed logarithmic-loss question. The source's surrounding paragraph concerns two-party internal information, despite the article's multiparty title. It already reports that compression without an overhead is impossible. The particular logarithmic factor, constant error, additive regularization and worst-case transcript-simulation guarantee below are specified here rather than attributed verbatim to its informal sentence.
definitions:
Alice has \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), Bob has \(y\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), and the pair \((X,Y)\) has an arbitrary probability distribution \(\mu\) on this finite product. The inputs may be correlated. Both parties know \(n\), the description of \(\pi\) and \(\mu\). Neither party is initially given the other party's realized input. No promise is placed on the support of \(\mu\).

A protocol uses one finite string \(R\) of shared fair random bits and two finite strings \(R_A,R_B\) of private fair random bits. The three strings are mutually independent and independent of \((X,Y)\). Their finite lengths may depend on the protocol and are not charged as communication. A length of zero is allowed. For each fixed public string, the protocol is a finite rooted binary communication tree: every internal node designates Alice or Bob, and the selected player sends one bit determined by their own input, private string, public string and the earlier messages. That bit selects the next child. A leaf terminates communication. The owner of the next message and termination are therefore determined by the public string and common message history, rather than by an uncharged timing channel. The transcript of communicated bits is \(M\), and the augmented transcript is \(T=(R,M)\). Both parties observe every communicated bit. A protocol is defined on every input pair and every coin choice. Its worst-case communication \(\operatorname{CC}(\pi)\) is the maximum number of transmitted bits over all these executions; it is finite but may be arbitrarily large.

All local computation, protocol descriptions and shared randomness are free. There is no restriction on the number of rounds or the local running time, and no privacy requirement. No advice depending on the other party's realized private input or quantum resources are supplied; all initial resources are exactly those specified above. Protocols for different \(n,\mu,\pi\) may be unrelated. This is an existence statement about finite communication protocols, not an efficient compiler for producing one from a table of \(\mu\).

For a finite random variable \(U\), its base-two Shannon entropy is
\[
H(U)=-\sum_{u}\Pr[U=u]\log_2\Pr[U=u],
\]
where \(0\log_2 0=0\). Conditional entropy \(H(U\mid V)\) is the average of \(H(U\mid V=v)\) weighted by \(\Pr[V=v]\), with zero-probability terms omitted. The conditional mutual information is
\[
I(U;W\mid V)=H(U\mid V)-H(U\mid V,W).
\]
The internal information cost in bits is
\[
I_{\mu}(\pi)=I(X;T\mid Y)+I(Y;T\mid X).
\]
All variables use the joint law of \(\mu\) and the three independent coin strings of \(\pi\). Including \(R\) in \(T\) accounts for public randomness; private coins are not included in that transcript. This is internal information, not the external quantity \(I(X,Y;T)\), and not the distinct multiparty public-information measure introduced in the source. The quantity is finite, nonnegative and at most \(2n\).

A simulation \(\rho\) is another finite protocol in the same model, with its own independent shared and private fair coins. At its terminal leaf Alice outputs a value \(T_A\) determined by her local view and Bob outputs \(T_B\) determined by his. These values lie in the finite set of augmented transcripts possible for \(\pi\), together with a failure symbol \(\bot\). Output descriptions and their lengths are not communication costs. The simulated public string of \(\pi\) is part of these output values; it need not equal \(\rho\)'s actual public string.

Let \(P\) be the law of \((X,Y,T,T)\) produced by drawing \((X,Y)\sim\mu\) and executing \(\pi\). Let \(Q\) be the law of \((X,Y,T_A,T_B)\) produced by drawing the same input distribution and executing \(\rho\). Regard both as distributions on the same finite product space, assigning zero mass to impossible original outcomes and to original failures. The simulation error is their total variation distance
\[
\operatorname{err}_{\mu}(\rho,\pi)=
\frac12\sum_{x,y,t_a,t_b}|P(x,y,t_a,t_b)-Q(x,y,t_a,t_b)|.
\]
Thus the requirement preserves correlation with the inputs and agreement between the parties' reconstructed transcripts, except for total variation at most \(1/100\). It is stronger than reproducing only an output bit of a particular function or only the unconditioned marginal law of \(T\). Error is averaged under \(\mu\) and the coins, whereas communication is worst case over every input pair and every coin string, including pairs of \(\mu\)-probability zero. There is no joint simulation of many independent copies. The \(+1\) in the cost bound avoids a zero-information boundary convention, and the logarithm is of the input bit length \(n\), not the number of possible inputs, the transcript length or the number of rounds.
answer_criterion:
Provide a complete, mathematically correct Lean proof of the universal compression statement or its full negation. Equivalently, a positive answer gives one absolute constant \(K\in\mathbb R,\ K\ge1\) and proves
\[
\forall n\ge1\ \forall\mu\ \forall\pi\ \exists\rho:\quad
\operatorname{err}_{\mu}(\rho,\pi)\le\frac1{100}
\ \land\
\operatorname{CC}(\rho)\le
K(I_{\mu}(\pi)+1)\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil.
\]
A negative answer must prove that for every proposed \(K\in\mathbb R,\ K\ge1\), there are \(n,\mu,\pi\) in the stated domain for which every simulation with error at most \(1/100\) has communication strictly larger than that bound. A positive theorem only for product input distributions or public-coin original protocols does not cover the universal domain, although a matching lower bound within either subclass can refute the universal statement. Refuting only constant-overhead compression does not refute the logarithmic allowance. An expected-communication upper bound must be converted to the specified worst-case guarantee; error slack and an increased absolute constant can permit such a conversion. A theorem for external or multiparty public information must establish the claimed conclusion for the internal-information measure defined here to qualify. Likewise, failure of one simulation construction is not a lower bound for all simulations. The chosen constant simulation error is part of the mathematical proposition; the benchmark asks for a proof of that proposition or negation, rather than an approximate numerical verdict.

title: Polynomial relation between classical and quantum communication
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: Two parties must evaluate a Boolean function when each holds one part of the input. The question asks whether randomized classical communication is polynomially bounded by quantum communication with shared entanglement for every total function. Both models allow bounded error on each input, and their costs count transmitted bits or qubits rather than local computation. August and September 2026 preprints claim total-function families with polylogarithmic quantum cost and polynomial randomized classical cost. Those stated results would refute the conjecture even with the quantum side allowed free entanglement, but their proofs are not independently certified in this review.
formal: Are randomized classical and entanglement-assisted quantum communication polynomially related for every total Boolean function? Precisely, do universal constants \(C\ge1\) and integer \(k\ge1\) exist such that \[R^{\mathrm{cc}}_{1/3}(F)\le C\bigl(Q^{\mathrm{cc},*}_{1/3}(F)+1\bigr)^k\] for every pair of nonempty finite sets \(X,Y\) and every function \(F:X\times Y\to\{0,1\}\)?
definitions: Alice receives \(x\in X\), Bob receives \(y\in Y\), and Bob must output \(F(x,y)\). A protocol is agreed in advance for the entire function \(F\). Local computation and storage are unrestricted and free; only communication is charged. The protocol may depend on \(F\), but its shared resources are independent of the actual inputs. In the classical model the parties exchange bits and may use shared public randomness and private randomness. In the quantum model they exchange qubits, may use arbitrary finite-dimensional local quantum operations and measurements, and may start with any finite-dimensional shared entangled state independent of \((x,y)\). There is no fixed upper bound on the amount of this prior entanglement; its preparation is not charged. Local quantum operations are completely positive trace-preserving maps, with measurement outcomes retained in local registers, and the final output is a two-outcome measurement at Bob. Classical bits sent by a quantum protocol count as transmitted qubits. Neither model receives free input-dependent advice or any communication through timing, message length, silence or postselection. One may use a fixed finite alternating schedule of transmissions, padding unused transmissions; local branches cannot signal through the schedule. Arbitrarily many rounds are allowed, with no input-length-dependent round restriction imposed by the question. The cost is the worst-case total number of bits or qubits transmitted, including all rounds and all randomness or measurement branches. In either model the output must equal \(F(x,y)\) with probability at least \(2/3\) on every pair \((x,y)\). The quantities \(R^{\mathrm{cc}}_{1/3}(F)\) and \(Q^{\mathrm{cc},*}_{1/3}(F)\) are the least costs among protocols with this guarantee. Total means that all of \(X\times Y\) is the correctness domain; no additional joint promise is allowed. The additive one in the polynomial handles zero-communication functions. The constants \(C,k\) must be independent of the function, the domains, any bit encoding of the inputs, and the amount of shared entanglement.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal polynomial bound or of its negation. A negative answer must show that for every \(C\ge1\) and integer \(k\ge1\), some finite total Boolean function satisfies \(R^{\mathrm{cc}}_{1/3}(F)>C(Q^{\mathrm{cc},*}_{1/3}(F)+1)^k\). A superpolynomial separating family can witness this; one fixed polynomial separation cannot. A bound with an extra input-length factor, a promise-problem or relation separation, or a comparison imposing a fixed round limit does not resolve the stated all-functions, unrestricted-round target.

title: Asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: A polynomial threshold function is the sign of a low-degree real polynomial on the Boolean cube. Total influence counts sensitive coordinates on average over uniform inputs. The conjecture asks for a universal bound proportional to degree times the square root of dimension. Its constant must be independent of both parameters. The stronger assertion identifying an exact symmetric maximizer is a different, disproved claim.
formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), every \(1\le d\le n\), and every Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\) represented as the sign of a real polynomial of degree at most \(d\), \[I(f)\le C d\sqrt n?\] Here \(I(f)\) is total influence, the expected number of input coordinates whose flip changes the output at a uniformly random input. The precise polynomial and tie conventions are defined below. The same constant must work for growing degrees as well as fixed degrees.
definitions:
Let \(\mathcal F_{n,d}\) denote the polynomial threshold functions specified below, and let \(M(n,d)=\max_{f\in\mathcal F_{n,d}}I(f)\). 

Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A real multilinear polynomial of degree at most \(d\) has the form
\[p(x)=\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[n]\\|S|\le d}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i,\qquad a_S\in\mathbb R,\]
with empty product \(1\). All coefficients are unrestricted reals; there is no bound on their magnitude, bit length, the number of nonzero monomials, or the minimum nonzero value of \(|p|\) on the cube. Require \(p(x)\ne0\) at every \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\). Its threshold function is \(f(x)=+1\) when \(p(x)>0\), and \(f(x)=-1\) when \(p(x)<0\). The class \(\mathcal F_{n,d}\) contains every function with at least one such representation, not just those whose least possible threshold degree is exactly \(d\). Starting with arbitrary real polynomials gives the same class: reducing powers using \(x_i^2=1\) preserves the cube values and does not increase degree. Excluding zeros fixes the tie convention; any representation using one fixed value of sign at zero can be perturbed by a sufficiently small constant to remove its cube zeros without changing the function.

Choose \(x\) uniformly from all \(2^n\) cube points, with independent equally likely coordinates. For \(i\in[n]\), let \(x^{\oplus i}\) have coordinate \(-x_i\) at \(i\) and agree with \(x\) elsewhere. Define
\[\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=2^{-n}|\{x:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\}|,\quad s_f(x)=|\{i\in[n]:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\}|,\]
\[I(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}s_f(x).\]
Thus total influence is average sensitivity, not maximum pointwise sensitivity and not influence divided by \(n\). There is no biased input distribution or additional probability over polynomials. The maximization is over Boolean functions; different coefficient choices representing the same function have the same influence. It is a maximum rather than merely a supremum because only finitely many Boolean functions exist on a fixed cube, and \(\mathcal F_{n,d}\) is nonempty. Constants belong to the class with influence zero, while a dictator \(f(x)=x_1\) has influence one; hence \(1\le M(n,d)\le n\) on the stated domain.

The constants in the answer must be absolute: they cannot depend on degree, dimension, a representation, or an asymptotic path through the parameter pairs. The estimates must hold throughout the domain, including small dimensions and growing degrees; finite exceptional cases must be covered by the proved constants. This is a mathematical extremal-growth problem, with no evaluation-time requirement or finite encoding assumption for real coefficients. The omitted degree-zero case has value zero, and degrees larger than \(n\) give no additional Boolean functions, so the displayed domain covers all nontrivial regimes.
answer_criterion: Prove in Lean that \(I(f)/(d\sqrt n)\) is bounded by one universal constant on the stated class of polynomial threshold functions, or show that this ratio is unbounded when \(n\) and \(d\) may vary.

title: Aanderaa–Karp–Rosenberg conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: An algorithm learns an unknown graph by asking whether individual pairs of vertices are edges. The conjecture asks whether every nonconstant monotone property invariant under vertex relabeling has some input requiring all possible pairs to be queried. Queries may be adaptive and all computation between them is free. The example of looking for one edge illustrates how an easy positive instance can coexist with an empty graph that requires a complete scan. The exact claim is known for prime-power vertex counts, while results about quantum queries, infinite graphs and broader topological symmetry must be distinguished from the full finite deterministic question.
formal: For every integer \(n\ge 2\) and every nonconstant function f from the simple undirected graphs on \([n]\) to \(\{0,1\}\) that is invariant under every permutation of \([n]\) and monotone under adding edges, is \(D(f)=n(n- 1)/2\), where \(D(f)\) is its deterministic worst-case adjacency-query complexity?
definitions: Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots ,n\}\) and \(U_{n}=\{\{i,j\}:1\le i<j\le n\}\). A graph is an arbitrary edge set \(E\subseteq U_{n}\), with no loops, parallel edges or input promises. Nonconstant means that f takes both values 0 and 1. Monotonicity means \(E\subseteq F\) implies \(f(E)\le f(F)\). Invariance means \(f(\pi (E))=f(E)\) for every permutation \(\pi\) of \([n]\), where \(\pi (E)=\{\{\pi (i),\pi (j)\}:\{i,j\}\in E\}\). A deterministic query algorithm is a finite rooted binary decision tree. Each internal node names an unordered pair in \(U_{n}\) and its two outgoing edges correspond to the answer 0 or 1 for absence or presence of that pair; each leaf carries an output bit. Following the answers supplied by E must end with output \(f(E)\) for every \(E\subseteq U_{n}\). The cost on E is the number of internal nodes visited, and \(D(f)\) is the minimum, over all such correct trees, of the maximum cost over E. Repeated queries can be omitted. The tree may depend arbitrarily on n and f; f is the fixed task, not an additional unknown input. Only queries count: computation, storage and the size of the tree are unrestricted, and no uniform procedure for constructing trees across n or f is required. The model is deterministic and exact, with no probability distribution over inputs. Reading every pair gives \(D(f)\le |U_{n}|\).
answer_criterion: Prove \(D(f)=|U_{n}|\) for every n and f satisfying the stated conditions, or refute this universal claim. A finite refutation consists of one n, a completely specified invariant nonconstant monotone f, and a correct decision tree whose depth is at most \(|U_{n}|- 1\). A lower bound only up to a constant factor, or a theorem restricted to particular properties or vertex counts, does not settle the full claim.

title: Constant-factor randomized direct sums for total Boolean functions
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: Alice and Bob must jointly compute a total Boolean function of their private inputs. The question compares the communication needed for one input pair with the communication needed for many pairs together. A single universal constant would force cost to grow proportionally with the number of copies. The protocol uses public randomness and must produce the entire answer vector correctly with probability at least two thirds on every input tuple. Recent claimed counterexamples for relations do not resolve the chosen total-function version.
formal: Is there an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that, for every pair of nonempty finite input sets \(X,Y\), every total Boolean function \(f:X\times Y\to\{0,1\}\) and every integer \(k\ge1\), \[R_{1/3}(f^{\otimes k})\ge c\,k\,R_{1/3}(f),\] where communication is public-coin, worst-case and measured with one global error probability?
definitions: Alice receives \(x\in X\) and Bob receives \(y\in Y\). Both know \(f\) and the finite domains. A public-coin protocol selects a deterministic binary communication tree using a finite string of independent shared fair random bits, independent of the inputs. At a node, the designated player sends one bit determined by that player’s own input, the public string and the transcript so far. At termination Bob outputs a bit determined by his input, the public string and transcript. The worst-case cost is the maximum number of communicated bits over all inputs and public strings. Local computation and the public random string are free; its finite length may depend on the protocol. There is no message to reveal the public seed, no advice depending on private inputs and no restriction to one-way communication. The complexity \(R_{1/3}(f)\) is the minimum cost of a protocol whose output equals \(f(x,y)\) with probability at least \(2/3\) on every input pair. It is finite because Alice can send an encoding of her input. Protocols may depend nonuniformly on the finite function; no uniform construction from its truth table is requested. For \(f^{\otimes k}:X^k\times Y^k\to\{0,1\}^k\), Alice and Bob receive their full tuples and Bob must output \((f(x_1,y_1),\ldots,f(x_k,y_k))\). Success probability at least \(2/3\) concerns the entire vector simultaneously on every tuple pair. The inputs need not be independent draws from a distribution: the cost and error guarantees are worst-case. The protocol may communicate across coordinates in any way. The constant \(c\) must work for all domains, functions and copy counts; a different constant for each fixed function is insufficient. Zero-communication functions impose the vacuous lower bound zero.
answer_criterion: Provide a Lean proof of the universal constant-factor inequality, or a Lean proof of its negation: for every positive proposed constant there are a total Boolean function and copy count violating it. Refuting a version for relations, partial functions, distributional inputs or per-coordinate error alone does not refute this selected assertion. Expected communication is not the cost used here.

title: Fixed-player number-on-forehead disjointness exponent
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
summary: In number-on-forehead communication, each player sees every input set except its own. The task is to decide whether all sets have empty common intersection. The card asks for the polynomial exponent of randomized communication in the universe size. Each fixed number of players has its own exponent, to absolute accuracy 0.01. Local computation is free and arbitrary interactive public broadcasts are allowed.
formal: For every fixed integer \(k\ge2\), determine to absolute error at most \(1/100\) the communication exponent \[x_{\mathrm{NOF}}(k)=\inf\{a\ge0:R(n,k)=O_k(n^a)\text{ as }n\to\infty\}.\] Here \(R(n,k)\) is the minimum worst-case public-coin randomized communication for deciding whether \(k\) subsets of \([n]\) have empty common intersection, with error at most \(1/3\); player \(i\) sees every set except the \(i\)-th. The full interactive broadcast model and asymptotic quantifiers are below.
definitions:
The universe \([n]\) is \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Each \(S_j\) is represented by its characteristic vector \(x^{(j)}\in\{0,1\}^n\), where \(x^{(j)}_t=1\) means \(t\in S_j\). There is no restriction on set sizes, intersections, repeated sets, or the number of players relative to \(n\). In particular, \(k\) can exceed \(n\). The predicate asks for an empty intersection of all sets, not pairwise disjointness. Equivalently, the complementary predicate asks whether some row of the \(n\)-by-\(k\) incidence matrix is all ones; complementing the common output leaves the communication complexity unchanged.

All players know \(n,k\), their labels and the protocol. Player \(i\)'s initial view is the ordered tuple \((x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(i-1)},x^{(i+1)},\ldots,x^{(k)})\). No player initially sees its missing column. This is the number-on-forehead model; it is different from giving player \(i\) only \(S_i\).

A deterministic protocol is a finite binary tree. An internal node specifies which player broadcasts the next bit. That bit can be any function of that player's visible input and the preceding public transcript. The bit is written once on a blackboard and is seen by all players; broadcasting one bit costs one bit, not \(k\) bits. Each leaf specifies a common output bit. The speaker and the decision to stop are determined by the public node, so they cannot transmit an uncharged input-dependent signal. The players may speak in any order prescribed by the tree and may return arbitrarily often; neither the number of rounds nor the number of messages is separately bounded.

A public-coin randomized protocol is a distribution over deterministic protocols, selected using shared randomness independent of the inputs. Its cost is the maximum depth of any tree in the support. This bound is over all inputs and all random outcomes, not an expectation. For every full input tuple, the probability that the common output equals \(\operatorname{DISJ}_{n,k}\) must be at least \(2/3\). No private communication, pre-shared secret or quantum resource is provided.

Local computation, storage and the complexity of the protocol description are free. Protocols may be chosen independently for each pair \((n,k)\); there is no uniform algorithm for generating them or local running-time requirement. The model therefore asks about communication alone.

Define \(R(n,k)\) to be the least integer \(d\ge0\) for which such a randomized protocol of cost at most \(d\) exists. This set of costs is nonempty: one player can transmit a missing column to another, who can broadcast the answer, using at most \(n+1\) bits. Both output values occur for every allowed \((n,k)\), so a zero-communication output independent of the input cannot attain error \(1/3\) on all inputs. Thus \(1\le R(n,k)\le n+1\).

For each fixed integer \(k\ge2\), define \[x_{\mathrm{NOF}}(k)=\inf\{a\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}:\exists C>0\ \exists n_0\ge1\ \forall n\ge n_0,\ R(n,k)\le Cn^a\}.\] The constant and threshold may depend on \(k\) and \(a\). The elementary bounds above ensure \(0\le x_{\mathrm{NOF}}(k)\le1\). The infimum need not be attained. The target does not require matching logarithmic factors, a uniform constant as \(k\) grows with \(n\), or a single protocol generator. Lower bounds must apply to all permitted randomized interactive protocols.
answer_criterion: Supply one explicitly described real-valued function \(a\) on all integer player counts \(k\ge2\). Prove in Lean that \(|a(k)-x_{\mathrm{NOF}}(k)|\le1/100\) at every point of that domain. A pair of [certified bounding functions](definitions.html#numerical-answers) \(L,U\) also qualifies if \(L(k)\le x_{\mathrm{NOF}}(k)\le U(k)\) and \(U(k)-L(k)\le1/50\) everywhere, with \(a=(L+U)/2\). At each fixed player count use the specified public-coin, worst-case communication measure.

title: Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis
summary: SETH asks whether the optimal deterministic exponential rates for fixed-width satisfiability approach one as the allowed width grows. Every proposed constant saving from exhaustive search must fail at some fixed width. To refute it, one saving must work at every fixed width, although the algorithms and polynomial factors may vary with that width. Faster algorithms for width three, including recent randomized ones, do not meet that requirement. The hypothesis underlies many precise conditional lower bounds, including problems whose algorithms already run in polynomial time.
formal: For every real \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), does there exist an integer \(q\ge3\) such that no q-SAT decider A has a bound \(t_A(F)\le C\,2^{(1-\varepsilon)n(F)}(N(F)+1)^d\) for every valid q-CNF formula F, for any fixed integers \(C\ge1,d\ge0\)? The width \(q\) may depend on \(\varepsilon\) but is fixed independently of the input. Equivalently, is \(\lim_{q\to\infty}s_q=1\)? This is the deterministic Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis.
definitions:
Use the shared [bounded-width CNF encoding and rate \(s_q\)](definitions.html#sat-encoding). The exponential term uses the number of distinct variables \(n(F)\). The polynomial factor uses the full input length \(N(F)\), including every repeated clause. The decider may depend on the fixed width \(q\).

The sequence \(s_q\) is nondecreasing: a decider for width q+1 also decides the width-q restriction after checking its syntax. Since every \(s_q\le1\), its limit exists. The quantified statement says that no fixed positive saving from the exponent 1 works for all fixed widths. Its negation is that there exists one real \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) such that for each integer \(q\ge3\) there are a q-SAT decider \(A_q\) and constants \(C_q,d_q\) with \(t_{A_q}(F)\le C_q2^{(1-\varepsilon)n(F)}(N(F)+1)^{d_q}\) for every q-CNF formula F. The algorithm and polynomial factor may depend on q and the selected \(\varepsilon\). There is no added requirement of one algorithm receiving q as an input, nor of an effective procedure generating \(A_q\) from q. Each individual machine is uniform over its formula inputs. Infima need not be attained; the equivalence uses the available slack between a limit below 1 and 1.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed deterministic all-width proposition, equivalently a proof that \(\lim_{q\to\infty}s_q=1\) or that this limit is strictly below 1. A refutation must establish one positive exponential saving valid at every fixed width, with the algorithm and polynomial factors allowed to depend on that width. A positive answer must exclude such a shared saving. Improvement at finitely many widths, a randomized algorithm, or a lower bound only under another unproved hypothesis does not by itself meet this criterion. The target is a yes/no assertion about the limit, not its numerical approximation.

title: Truly subquadratic algorithms for 3SUM
summary: 3SUM asks whether a value in one integer list is the sum of values from two other lists. The target is a fixed polynomial improvement over quadratic running time on a precisely specified word RAM. The selected variant allows every fixed polynomial integer universe and requires a common exponent saving. Randomization may change the running time but must never produce an incorrect answer. Known logarithmic savings and faster queries after preprocessing do not meet the from-scratch target.
formal:
Is there a constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) such that, for every fixed integer \(B\ge1\), a uniform randomized Las Vegas algorithm solves integer 3SUM with worst-case expected time \(O(n^{2-\varepsilon})\) on the word RAM defined below? An input consists of three lists \(A,B',C\), each containing at most \(n\) integers in \([-n^B,n^B]\), and the task is to decide whether
\[\exists a\in A\ \exists b\in B'\ \exists c\in C:\quad a+b=c.\]
The algorithm and hidden constant may depend on the fixed universe exponent \(B\); the saving \(\varepsilon\) must be independent of \(B\). This selects the polynomial-universe integer version of the source's question, with the expected-time convention used by Kopelowitz–Pettie–Porat.
definitions:
The size parameter \(n\ge2\) bounds the length of each of the three lists. Repeated values are allowed and do not affect the answer; each chosen value comes from its prescribed list. A triple may contain equal numerical values from different lists. There is no single-list distinctness condition. Integers are supplied explicitly in signed binary and fit in one word of
\[w=\left\lceil(B+3)\log_2(n+1)\right\rceil\]
bits. The target equation is equality of ordinary integers, not congruence modulo the word size.

For each fixed \(B\), a uniform word-RAM algorithm has a finite program independent of \(n\) and of all list contents. Its memory cells contain \(w\)-bit words and are addressed by words. Initially only the input and its lengths are present; other cells are zero. Unit-cost instructions are reading or writing a word, copying, comparing, branching, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), integer quotient and remainder for a nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and shifts by a word-specified amount; a shift by at least \(w\) yields zero. Division by zero can be defined to return zero. The program may obtain an independent uniformly random \(w\)-bit word at unit cost. There is no arbitrary-precision unit-cost arithmetic, real-number operation, oracle or nonuniform lookup table. Any table construction, sorting and preprocessing count toward the runtime. Arithmetic on more than one word must be implemented by these instructions.

Las Vegas means that the program halts with probability one and every output produced is correct; randomization affects its runtime, not its answer. The required bound means that for each \(B\) there are \(K_B,n_B\) such that the expected number of instructions is at most \(K_B n^{2-\varepsilon}\) on every valid instance with \(n\ge n_B\). Expectation is over the program's random words, followed by a worst case over the input lists. All smaller valid instances must also be decided correctly with finite expected time. No average-case input distribution or reusable preprocessing is supplied.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the existence claim, including one positive exponent saving uniform over every fixed \(B\), correctness, almost-sure termination and the expected instruction bound; or prove its negation. Negation means that for every \(\varepsilon>0\) some fixed polynomial universe admits no algorithm meeting that saving. An improvement by logarithmic factors alone, a fast data-structure query after expensive preprocessing, a restricted comparison-tree lower bound, or a Monte Carlo algorithm without the stipulated zero-error guarantee does not settle this selected target.

title: Subexponential-time Circuit-SAT
summary: The input is an explicitly listed Boolean circuit with no depth or sharing restriction. The task is to decide exactly whether some assignment to its input variables makes the output true. One deterministic algorithm must run in \(2^{o(n)}\operatorname{poly}(L)\) time, where \(n\) counts input variables and \(L\) is the full encoding length. The polynomial overhead is fixed for all circuit sizes, so a result only for linear-size circuits or fixed-width formulas does not establish the target. A complete Lean-checked proof of the existence claim or its unconditional negation is required.
formal:
Does there exist one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\), an integer \(d\ge1\), a constant \(K\ge1\), and a function \(g:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with \(\lim_{n\to\infty}g(n)/n=0\), such that \(A\) decides satisfiability of every explicitly given Boolean circuit with \(n\ge1\) input variables and \(s\ge0\) gates in at most
\[
K\,2^{g(n)}(N+1)^d
\]
Turing-machine bit steps? Here \(N\) is the full binary encoding length, gates are binary AND and OR and unary NOT, and depth and fan-out are unrestricted. The output must be correct on every circuit. The requested bound is abbreviated \(2^{o(n)}\operatorname{poly}(N)\); its exponential parameter is the number of input variables, not the number of gates or encoding bits.
definitions:
